In autonomous multi-agent networks, agents must be able to discover each other's capabilities dynamically while verifying that an agent's declared schemas, endpoints, and credentials have not been tampered with in transit. Under the Linux Foundation A2A specification, each autonomous agent publishes an Agent Card at a well-known URL. GoRoute AI Gateway acts as a secure identity proxy, enforcing RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) and RFC 7515 JSON Web Signature (JWS) signing and verification. Cryptographic Pipeline Raw JSON Upstream Agent(Publishes Agent Card) GoRoute AI Gateway Signer GET /.well-known/agent-card.json(Signed Agent Card) RFC 8785 JCS Canonicalization(Deterministic Lexicographical Order) SHA-256 Digest RFC 7515 JWS Signing(ES256, RS256, EdDSA)

Clients and external agent swarms discover agent capabilities via the well-known discovery route: # Discover default gateway agent card curl -X GET "http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent-card.json" # Discover a specific registered agent by slug curl -X GET "http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent-card.json?agent=risk-analyst"

{ "name": "Risk Analysis Agent", "description": "Autonomous financial risk evaluation and stress-testing agent.", "version": "1.0.0", "supportedInterfaces": [ { "protocolBinding": "HTTP+JSON", "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst" }, { "protocolBinding": "JSON-RPC", "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst" }, { "protocolBinding": "GRPC", "url": "localhost:9090" } ], "capabilities": { "streaming": true, "pushNotifications": true, "statePersistence": true }, "signature": { "alg": "ES256", "kid": "gw-a2a-signer-v1", "jws": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Imd3LWEyYS1zaWduZXItdjEifQ.eyJjYXBhYmlsaXRpZXMi...signature" } }

Standard JSON encoders do not guarantee deterministic serialization: key ordering is arbitrary, whitespace varies, and numeric representations differ across platforms. Without canonical serialization, cryptographic signatures fail. GoRoute AI Gateway implements RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) (internal/a2a/card.go): Lexicographical Key Sorting: Object member names are sorted lexicographically by Unicode code point values. Whitespace Stripping: Eliminates all non-essential formatting whitespace outside string literals. Canonical Number Formatting: Integers and arbitrary-precision floats are represented without exponents when within safe ranges, preserving decimal precision. UTF-8 Character Escaping: Only essential control characters (", \) are escaped. // CanonicalizeJCS serializes any JSON-compatible object into RFC 8785 JCS. func CanonicalizeJCS(v any) ([]byte, error) { raw, err := json.Marshal(v) if err != nil { return nil, err } var parsed any dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw)) dec.UseNumber() if err := dec.Decode(&parsed); err != nil { return nil, err } return canonicalizeValue(parsed) }
Once canonicalized, the card payload is signed according to RFC 7515 JSON Web Signature (JWS).

The gateway supports three standard asymmetric signing algorithms configured in configs/config.yaml: ES256 (Default): ECDSA with the NIST P-256 curve and SHA-256. Recommended for modern high-performance cloud environments. RS256: RSA signature with SHA-256 (minimum 2048-bit key). EdDSA: Ed25519 high-speed elliptic curve signature scheme.

The signature is formatted in compact 3-part Base64URL notation: BASE64URL(UTF8(ProtectedHeader)) . BASE64URL(JCS(Payload)) . BASE64URL(SignatureBytes) Where the Protected Header declares the algorithm and key ID: { "alg": "ES256", "kid": "gw-a2a-signer-v1" }

When GoRoute AI Gateway proxies an external or upstream A2A agent: Upstream Ingestion: The gateway fetches the upstream agent card and validates its cryptographic signature against the upstream's published JWKS. Endpoint Rewriting: Upstream interface URLs (e.g. http://internal-agent-host:3000) are rewritten to point to the gateway's unified ingress proxy (https://gateway.acme.com/a2a/v1/agents/{slug}). Re-Signing: Because rewriting modifies the payload, the gateway strips the old signature, canonicalizes the updated payload via RFC 8785 JCS, and re-signs the document using the gateway's private key (a2a.signing_key_id). This guarantees that downstream clients can verify the authenticity of the card while directing all live traffic through the gateway's rate limiters, FinOps ledgers, and security guardrails.

a2a: enabled: true signing_key_id: "gw-a2a-signer-v1" allowed_signing_algs: - "ES256" - "RS256" - "EdDSA" # Upstream trusted agent public JWKS keys trusted_card_jwks: "risk-analyst": "https://risk-agent.partner.com/.well-known/jwks.json" "compliance-bot": "https://compliance.internal.bank/.well-known/jwks.json" [!IMPORTANT] In production environments, never set a2a.allow_legacy_card_discovery: true. All agent cards must be cryptographically signed and verifiable against approved keys to prevent man-in-the-middle capability spoofing.

GoRoute AI Gateway enables seamless interoperability between autonomous A2A agents and existing AI application ecosystems: OpenAI Compatibility Bridge (model: "a2a/{slug}"): Exposes autonomous agents over standard POST /v1/chat/completions, allowing off-the-shelf OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Cursor, Claude Code, and OpenWebUI to call A2A agents without custom protocol libraries. Native gRPC Service (lf.a2a.v1.A2AService): High-performance, low-latency Protobuf RPCs with server-side streaming designed for production microservice architectures. Diverse Client Ecosystem GoRoute AI Gateway Autonomous Agents POST /v1/chat/completions POST /v1/chat/completions gRPC Channel: 9090 OpenAI Python / Node SDK(model: 'a2a/risk-analyst') LangChain / LlamaIndex Internal Go / Java Microservice(Native gRPC Client) OpenAI Bridge Handler(internal/a2a/openai_bridge.go) A2A gRPC Server(lf.a2a.v1.A2AService) 4-Layer RBAC Engine A2A Router Service Risk Analyst Agent Worker
The OpenAI Compatibility Bridge translates standard Chat Completions requests into A2A agent tasks, preserving conversational state, streaming SSE chunks, and enforcing tenant permissions.

To invoke an agent named risk-analyst, simply set model to "a2a/risk-analyst": curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "a2a/risk-analyst", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Perform sensitivity analysis on portfolio beta under a 200bps rate hike." } ], "stream": false }' Response Format​ The gateway formats the agent's task output into standard OpenAI response JSON: { "id": "chatcmpl_a2a_task_01928374", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 1731340800, "model": "a2a/risk-analyst", "choices": [ { "index": 0, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "### Portfolio Sensitivity Analysis\nUnder a 200bps rate increase, duration-sensitive fixed income assets experience an estimated 4.2% drawdown while high-dividend equity beta contracts by 0.15..." }, "finish_reason": "stop" } ], "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 38, "completion_tokens": 154, "total_tokens": 192 } }

Existing code using the official openai Python package works without code changes: from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1", api_key="sk-gw-client-key" ) # Call the autonomous agent directly response = client.chat.completions.create( model="a2a/risk-analyst", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "Analyze supply chain risks for our automotive supplier portfolio."} ], stream=True ) for chunk in response: content = chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "" print(content, end="", flush=True)

To continue an existing agent task across multiple turns, pass the task identifier via HTTP headers or metadata: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "X-Gateway-Task-Id: task_01928374-abcd-ef01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "a2a/risk-analyst", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Re-run the previous stress test assuming high inflation persistency."} ] }'
For backend systems, microservices, and Kubernetes clusters requiring high-throughput binary serialization, GoRoute AI Gateway exposes the native Linux Foundation A2A gRPC service.

syntax = "proto3"; package lf.a2a.v1; service A2AService { // Dispatches a message to an agent task rpc SendMessage(SendMessageRequest) returns (SendMessageResponse); // Queries task status, current state, and artifacts rpc GetTask(GetTaskRequest) returns (Task); // Lists active tasks for the authenticated caller rpc ListTasks(ListTasksRequest) returns (ListTasksResponse); // Signals cancellation to an in-flight agent task rpc CancelTask(CancelTaskRequest) returns (Task); // Real-time server-streaming of task progress events rpc SubscribeToTask(SubscribeToTaskRequest) returns (stream StreamResponse); // Webhook push notification configurations rpc CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig(TaskPushNotificationConfig) returns (TaskPushNotificationConfig); rpc GetTaskPushNotificationConfig(GetTaskPushNotificationConfigRequest) returns (TaskPushNotificationConfig); rpc DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig(DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfigRequest) returns (google.protobuf.Empty); }

gRPC clients authenticate by including the standard VirtualKey Bearer token in the gRPC incoming metadata context: md := metadata.Pairs( "authorization", "Bearer sk-gw-client-key-prod", "agent-slug", "risk-analyst", ) ctx := metadata.NewOutgoingContext(context.Background(), md) The gateway extracts the token, executes the 4-layer RBAC policy check, and attributes compute spend to the associated organization and team.

package main import ( "context" "fmt" "io" "log" "github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/internal/a2a/pb" "google.golang.org/grpc" "google.golang.org/grpc/credentials/insecure" "google.golang.org/grpc/metadata" ) func main() { conn, err := grpc.Dial("localhost:9090", grpc.WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials())) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("did not connect: %v", err) } defer conn.Close() client := pb.NewA2AServiceClient(conn) ctx := metadata.NewOutgoingContext(context.Background(), metadata.Pairs( "authorization", "Bearer sk-gw-client-key-prod", )) stream, err := client.SubscribeToTask(ctx, &pb.SubscribeToTaskRequest{ TaskId: "task_01928374", AfterSeq: 0, }) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("subscribe failed: %v", err) } for { event, err := stream.Recv() if err == io.EOF { break } if err != nil { log.Fatalf("stream error: %v", err) } fmt.Printf("[Seq %d] Event: %s, Payload: %s\n", event.EventSeq, event.EventType, event.PayloadJson) } } [!TIP] Use lf.a2a.v1.A2AService when building backend services that require sub-millisecond serialization overhead and high-volume parallel event streaming.

The Linux Foundation Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A v1.0) is an open, vendor-neutral specification governing autonomous multi-agent communication, collaborative task execution, and real-time event distribution. GoRoute AI Gateway implements an enterprise-grade A2A router and messaging hub, enabling independent agent systems (e.g., LangChain agents, AutoGen swarms, Claude Code, and autonomous background bots) to coordinate tasks securely with enterprise auth, audit trails, and multi-tenant isolation. Client Agents GoRoute AI Gateway Hub Target Agent Network HTTP POST or JSON-RPC Events GET :subscribe SSE HTTP Webhook Push Initiator Agent A Client Bot B Dual Ingress Binding(HTTP+JSON & JSON-RPC 2.0) A2A Task Router Service Subscribe-First SSE Engine(Monotonic Event Sequences) Transactional Outbox Worker(DLQ & Exponential Backoff) Autonomous Worker Agent C Webhook Subscriber D
To ensure compatibility across different software ecosystems, GoRoute AI Gateway exposes identical agent capabilities over two transport bindings:
documents.s: 1. Dual Protocol Binding: HTTP+JSON and JSON-RPC 2.0

documents.t: Idiomatic REST APIs designed for standard HTTP microservices and web clients: Operation Method & Route Description Send Message POST /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}/messages Submits a message to an agent, initializing or continuing a task. Get Task GET /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}/tasks/{taskID} Retrieves current task status, artifacts, and execution state. List Tasks GET /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}/tasks Lists active and historical tasks for the caller. Cancel Task POST /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}/tasks/{taskID}:cancel Signals cancellation to an in-flight agent task. Subscribe Stream GET /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}/tasks/{taskID}:subscribe Opens a real-time SSE stream of task events.

Standardized RPC interface accessible on a single URL (POST /a2a/v1/agents/{slug}): curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 101, "method": "sendMessage", "params": { "message": { "role": "user", "content": "Evaluate quarterly exposure to semiconductor supply shocks." } } }' Supported JSON-RPC methods: sendMessage, getTask, listTasks, cancelTask, createPushConfig, getPushConfig, deletePushConfig.

A common vulnerability in distributed SSE streaming is the "race window": if a client queries the database for past events and then connects to the live stream, any event emitted between the database read and the socket connection is permanently lost. GoRoute AI Gateway implements the Subscribe-First SSE Protocol (internal/a2a/streams.go): 1. GET /tasks/{id}:subscribe?after_seq=4 2. Subscribe(gw:a2a:events:{id}) 3. HTTP 200 text/event-stream 4. ListEvents(taskID, seq > 4) 5. Historical Events (seq 5, 6) 6. SSE id: 5, id: 6 7. Live Event (seq 8) [Gap: seq 7 missing] 8. Fetch Missing Gap (seq 7) 9. Event 7 Payload 10. SSE id: 7 11. SSE id: 8 1. Subscribe to Redis FIRST 2. Backfill Historical Events 3. Gap Detection & Backfill Subscriber Client Gateway SSE Handler Redis Pub/Sub PostgreSQL (a2a_events)

Subscribe-First Sequencing: Connects to the Redis event channel gw:a2a:events:{taskID} before fetching database snapshots, buffering live events in a channel. Monotonic Event Sequencing: Every task event is assigned an auto-incrementing 64-bit integer sequence number (id: 1, id: 2, id: 3). Resumption via Last-Event-ID: If a subscriber disconnects, it reconnects with standard Last-Event-ID: <seq> or ?after_seq=<seq>. The gateway replays all missed events seamlessly. Gap Detection & Deduplication: If a live buffered event skips a sequence number, the gateway queries PostgreSQL to backfill the missing gap before delivering live events. Duplicate events already delivered during backfill are discarded. Periodic Keep-Alive: Emits comment frames (: keepalive\n\n) every 15 seconds to prevent intermediate proxy timeout disconnects.

For asynchronous event delivery to external systems, the gateway implements a Transactional Outbox Worker (internal/a2a/outbox_worker.go). Background Outbox Worker Atomic Transaction Yes No (under 5 retries) No (max retries exceeded) Agent Task Mutation PostgreSQL1. Task Event2. a2a_outbox_events Status: SENT Exponential Backoff100ms * 2^attempt Status: DEAD_LETTER (DLQ) Claim Pending Batches (50 events) HTTP POST with Idempotency-Key Delivery Success?

Zero-Loss Transactions: The task status mutation and the outbound webhook event are written within the same database transaction. Events can never be lost due to process crashes. Idempotency & Attribution Headers: Outbound webhook POSTs carry strict idempotency and audit metadata: POST /webhooks/agent-events HTTP/1.1 Host: client-service.acme.com Content-Type: application/json Idempotency-Key: evt_01928374-abcd-ef01 X-Gateway-Event-Id: evt_01928374-abcd-ef01 X-Gateway-Task-Id: task_98765432-feed-dead X-Gateway-Delivery-Attempt: 1 Exponential Backoff: Failed deliveries back off exponentially (100ms * 2^attempt). Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ): After 5 consecutive failures (a2a.max_push_retries: 5), the event status transitions to dead_letter for operator inspection. Emergency Kill-Switch: Webhook delivery can be deactivated instantly per agent or globally by deleting or toggling push notification configs.

GoRoute AI Gateway provides multiple architectural execution paths for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools: Virtual Hub Aggregation (POST /mcp): Aggregates all registered tools in an organization behind a single JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint with automatic namespace prefixing. Scoped Server Execution (POST /mcp/{slug}): Direct JSON-RPC 2.0 execution routed to a specific registered server without prefix requirements. Curated Toolsets (POST /mcp/toolsets/{slug}): Scoped execution across pre-approved, team-specific subsets of tools. Plain REST Bridge (/mcp-rest/*): High-performance HTTP REST endpoints (GET /mcp-rest/tools/list and POST /mcp-rest/tools/call) designed for standard REST clients, completely decoupling applications from JSON-RPC protocol boilerplate. POST /mcp POST /mcp/{slug} POST /mcp/toolsets/{slug} GET / POST /mcp-rest/* Client / Agent Gateway Ingress Virtual Hub (All Servers Aggregated) Scoped Server Route Curated Toolset Route Plain REST Bridge Transport Dispatcher MCP Server A MCP Server B OpenAPI REST Target
documents.s: MCP Virtual Hub & Plain REST Bridge

documents.t: The Virtual Hub merges tools from all active MCP servers in the caller's organization.

To discover all callable tools across all connected servers: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }' Response with Namespaced Prefixes​ The gateway prefixes each tool name with its server slug ({serverSlug}__{toolName}) to prevent collisions: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "tools": [ { "name": "postgres-db__run_query", "description": "Execute read-only SQL queries on the replica database.", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["sql"] } }, { "name": "github-ops__create_pull_request", "description": "Create a new pull request in repository.", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" }, "branch": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["title", "branch"] } } ] } }

Execute an aggregated tool by referencing its prefixed name: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "postgres-db__run_query", "arguments": { "sql": "SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users LIMIT 5;" } } }' The gateway extracts the prefix postgres-db, resolves the server credentials and network transport, and dispatches the call to the target server.

When an agent needs to communicate exclusively with one server (such as an internal Jira or Kubernetes MCP server), use the scoped endpoint: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp/github-ops" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }' In scoped mode: Tool names are presented unprefixed (e.g., create_pull_request rather than github-ops__create_pull_request). Execution is isolated strictly to the target server, reducing fan-out overhead.

A Toolset is a curated collection of specific tools drawn from one or more MCP servers. Toolsets allow organizations to enforce principle-of-least-privilege access: Example: An analyst-toolset might expose postgres-db__run_query and slack__post_message, but hide postgres-db__drop_table and aws__terminate_instance. curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp/toolsets/analyst-toolset" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }'
For client applications, web frontends, or microservices that prefer standard HTTP REST semantics over JSON-RPC 2.0 envelopes, the gateway provides the Plain REST Bridge.

Retrieve available tools as a clean JSON array: # List all tools in organization curl -X GET "http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/list" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" # Filter tools to a specific server curl -X GET "http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/list?server_slug=postgres-db" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" Response​ { "tools": [ { "id": "tool_019283", "server_id": "srv_pg_prod", "name": "run_query", "description": "Execute read-only SQL queries on the replica database.", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["sql"] } } ] }

Invoke a tool with a standard JSON body without JSON-RPC version headers or ID matching: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/call" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "server_slug": "postgres-db", "tool_name": "run_query", "arguments": { "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';" } }' Successful Execution Response​ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "{\"count\": 42}" } ], "is_error": false }

If a caller provides tool_name without specifying server_slug, and that tool name exists across multiple connected MCP servers, the REST bridge safely rejects the call with HTTP 400 (AmbiguousToolName) rather than executing unpredictably: { "error": { "code": "AmbiguousToolName", "message": "Tool name \"run_query\" exists on multiple servers; server_slug is required.", "tool_name": "run_query", "matching_servers": ["postgres-db", "snowflake-warehouse"] } } [!TIP] Use the Plain REST Bridge when building internal tools, web dashboards, or microservices that need to call MCP tools via standard fetch(), Axios, or Go http.Client without pulling in complex JSON-RPC dependencies.

GoRoute AI Gateway is the first enterprise AI data plane with native, multi-version support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specifications. It unifies distributed tools, databases, APIs, and command-line utilities behind a resilient, high-speed gateway hub. Client / Agent(Claude Code, Cursor, Custom Agent) GoRoute AI Gateway(Virtual Hub POST /mcp & REST /mcp-rest) Remote MCP Server A(Streamable HTTP 2026-07-28 Stateless) Legacy MCP Server B(HTTP-SSE 2025-11-25 Stateful) Legacy MCP Server C(HTTP-SSE 2024-11-05 Bidirectional) Local Stdio Tool(Sandboxed Subprocess)

The gateway implements a multi-version transport dispatcher that detects and adapts protocol nuances seamlessly across MCP server generations. Specification Transport Layer Session Model Key Characteristics MCP 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP (Stateless) Stateless Zero initialization handshake, no session affinity or cookie requirements, direct JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST. MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP (Stateful) Stateful Session ID Requires Mcp-Session-Id header tracking, Redis session maps, heartbeat keep-alive, 15-minute inactivity TTL. MCP 2024-11-05 HTTP + SSE (Legacy) Long-Lived Stream Bidirectional Server-Sent Events stream (GET /sse) paired with HTTP POST message submission channel. Stdio Subprocess Standard I/O Pipes Process-Bound Executes local command-line tools in isolated child processes with environment scrubbing and binary allowlists.

The modern 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP specification represents the cloud-native standard for enterprise tool calling: Zero Protocol-Level Handshake: Eliminates the mandatory initialize $\rightarrow$ initialized round-trip handshake prior to calling tools. Direct POST Routing: Every tool execution is an independent HTTP POST request bearing standard JSON-RPC 2.0 payloads. Horizontal Scalability: Because requests are completely stateless, any gateway pod in a Kubernetes cluster can handle any tool call without sticky sessions or centralized session affinity routing.

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/mcp" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "postgres__run_query", "arguments": { "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users;" } } }'
For upstream MCP servers implementing older protocol specifications, the gateway provides automatic backwards-compatibility adapters.

Session Lifecycle Management: Maps upstream Mcp-Session-Id values in Redis with automatic 15-minute inactivity timeouts (mcp.session_ttl_minutes: 15). Heartbeat & Keep-Alive Daemon: Periodically dispatches JSON-RPC ping requests to prevent upstream server timeout disconnects. Principal Digest Validation: Validates cryptographic hashes of client virtual keys to ensure one client cannot hijack another client's MCP session.

Bidirectional SSE Tunneling: Establishes a persistent text/event-stream listener against legacy upstream SSE endpoints, extracting tool emission events into internal Go channels. POST Bridge Routing: Translates incoming gateway tool calls into upstream SSE postback requests, returning results synchronously to the client.

Instead of configuring clients with individual URLs for each MCP service, GoRoute AI Gateway acts as an enterprise Virtual Hub: Consolidated Endpoint (POST /mcp): Clients connect to a single gateway endpoint. The gateway queries all registered upstream MCP servers in parallel, merges their tool schemas, and presents a single unified tool manifest. Namespace Collision Prevention: Avoids naming conflicts across servers by prefixing tool names with the server slug: {serverSlug}__{toolName} (e.g. github__create_issue, gitlab__create_issue). Partial Failure Isolation: If one upstream MCP server is unreachable or offline, the virtual hub isolates the fault and returns tools from healthy servers without dropping the entire request. Curated Toolsets (POST /mcp/toolsets/{slug}): Group tools across disparate servers into domain-specific collections (e.g. devops-tools, finance-tools) restricted by 4-layer RBAC.

Standard JSON parsers convert numeric values into IEEE-754 64-bit floating-point numbers, leading to precision loss in financial transactions, cryptographic IDs, and micro-dollar accounting. GoRoute AI Gateway parses all MCP tool payloads using Go's json.Number and math/big.Rat, guaranteeing zero rounding errors or precision drift across high-precision numbers.

For operations returning extensive data sets, the gateway issues single-use, AEAD-encrypted continuation tokens: Identity Bound: Cryptographically tied to the caller's virtual key and organization ID. TTL Enforced: Expires automatically after 5 minutes to prevent replay attacks. Memory Optimized: Large intermediate tool results are spooled to temporary storage rather than held in hot memory.

The gateway inspects tool schemas discovered from external servers: Schema Sanitization: Scans descriptions and parameter names for prompt injection payloads. Cryptographic Tool Pinning: Computes a SHA-256 fingerprint (ToolDefHash) for every registered tool schema. If an upstream server silently mutates its schema without administrative approval, the gateway suspends execution fail-closed.

In enterprise AI deployments, organizations frequently integrate dozens of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and external APIs, resulting in catalogs spanning hundreds or thousands of callable tools. Directly serializing every tool's complete JSON Schema into an LLM's system prompt introduces severe operational bottlenecks: Massive Context Consumption: 100+ complete tool definitions consume between 20,000 to 50,000 input tokens per inference request. FinOps Inefficiencies: Sending massive schemas on every chat turn exponentially inflates API costs. Model Attention Degradation: Overly long system prompts impair the model's ability to focus on user instructions and reasoning steps. Security & Poisoning Risks: Exposing internal database structures and schemas upfront increases exposure to indirect prompt injection attacks. GoRoute AI Gateway solves this challenge through MCP Progressive Tool Discovery, a token-efficient architecture using compact 256-bit opaque handles (tool_hdl_...), an enterprise registry feed (GET /v1/goroute/mcp/registry), schema hydration meta-tools, and governed OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 transport.

1. GET /v1/goroute/mcp/registry 2. Lightweight Feed (Name & tool_hdl) 3. POST /v1/chat/completions (search_tools) 4. Compact Matches with Opaque Handles 5. POST /mcp (get_tool_schema) 6. Resolve Handle & Verify Hash 7. Verified Handle Record 8. Full Input JSON Schema 9. POST /mcp (Execute tool call) 10. Forward Tool Invocation 11. Tool Result Payload 12. Execution Response Agent selects required tool Client / Agent GoRoute AI Gateway Redis Fabric (L2) Upstream MCP Server Instead of sending full schemas upfront, the gateway supplies the LLM with two lightweight meta-tools (search_tools and get_tool_schema), allowing the agent to discover and hydrate only the exact schemas required for the immediate task.
When tools are indexed by the gateway, the ProgressiveDiscoveryManager generates a cryptographically random 256-bit handle with the tool_hdl_ prefix.

const ( HandlePrefix = "tool_hdl_" HandleTTL = 1 * time.Hour RedisHdlPrefix = "gw:mcp:hdl:" ) // ToolHandleRecord stores the binding between a 256-bit opaque handle and a verified tool. type ToolHandleRecord struct { Handle string `json:"handle"` ToolID string `json:"tool_id"` ServerID string `json:"server_id"` ServerSlug string `json:"server_slug"` ToolName string `json:"tool_name"` SchemaHash string `json:"schema_hash"` OrgID string `json:"org_id"` CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"` ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"` } Each handle is backed by 32 bytes (256 bits) of cryptographically secure random entropy (crypto/rand), yielding a 64-character hex string: tool_hdl_a4f91c0e38b29d47c6e11894a3bc76d892015fa43d67bc1e89e02345fa6712bc

Handles have a 1-hour TTL (HandleTTL = 1 * time.Hour) and are cached in Redis under gw:mcp:hdl:{handle}. When an agent presents a handle to hydrate a schema, the gateway performs strict cryptographic freshness verification: The gateway looks up the ToolHandleRecord in Redis or in-memory fallback. The gateway retrieves the current tool definition from the repository database. The gateway compares the tool's SHA-256 schema hash (tool.ToolDefHash) with the recorded hash in the handle (record.SchemaHash). If an upstream administrator has updated or modified the tool schema during the session, the gateway rejects the request with ErrStaleToolHandle: if tool.ToolDefHash != record.SchemaHash { return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: handle schema hash %s does not match repository hash %s", ErrStaleToolHandle, record.SchemaHash, tool.ToolDefHash) } [!IMPORTANT] Fail-closed freshness verification prevents race conditions and schema injection: an agent cannot execute a cached tool if the underlying schema or permissions have been altered while the handle was in flight.

Client applications and autonomous frameworks can retrieve the entire registered tool catalog without schemas using the registry feed endpoint: curl -X GET "http://localhost:8080/v1/goroute/mcp/registry" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-client-key-production"

[ { "server_slug": "postgres-service", "server_name": "Production Read-Replica DB", "transport_type": "streamable_http", "protocol_version": "2026-07-28", "endpoint_url": "https://mcp-pg.internal.acme.com/mcp", "tool_count": 2, "tools": [ { "name": "run_read_query", "server_slug": "postgres-service", "description": "Executes read-only SQL queries against the analytics database.", "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_8f93a1c0d45b7e82910fa32456bc718293041fa982345bc78129034fa9812bc4" }, { "name": "explain_query_plan", "server_slug": "postgres-service", "description": "Generates query execution plans without running mutations.", "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_1029384756afbecd0192837465fabcde0192837465afbecd0192837465afbecd" } ] }, { "server_slug": "github-actions", "server_name": "CI/CD Pipeline Automation", "transport_type": "openapi", "protocol_version": "2026-07-28", "endpoint_url": "https://api.github.com", "tool_count": 1, "tools": [ { "name": "trigger_workflow", "server_slug": "github-actions", "description": "Triggers automated test and deployment workflow runs.", "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566" } ] } ]
When connecting an LLM to the gateway via progressive discovery, the gateway exposes two core meta-tools:

Allows the agent to search for tools based on intent or query terms: { "name": "search_tools", "description": "Searches the enterprise tool catalog for matching capabilities and returns lightweight tool summaries with opaque handles.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "query": { "type": "string", "description": "Keyword search query (e.g. 'postgres', 'sql', 'deploy', 'analytics')" }, "limit": { "type": "integer", "description": "Maximum number of results to return (default 10, max 50)" } }, "required": ["query"] } }

Fetches the complete JSON Schema definition for a specific tool using its opaque handle: { "name": "get_tool_schema", "description": "Hydrates and returns the authoritative JSON inputSchema for a specific tool using its 256-bit opaque handle.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "tool_handle": { "type": "string", "description": "The opaque handle starting with 'tool_hdl_' obtained from search_tools or the registry feed." } }, "required": ["tool_handle"] } }

When the LLM invokes get_tool_schema with handle tool_hdl_8f93a1c0d45b7e82910fa32456bc718293041fa982345bc78129034fa9812bc4, the gateway responds: { "name": "run_read_query", "server_slug": "postgres-service", "description": "Executes read-only SQL queries against the analytics database.", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string", "description": "The SQL SELECT statement to execute." }, "max_rows": { "type": "integer", "description": "Maximum rows to return.", "default": 100 } }, "required": ["sql"] } } Now, the agent holds only the single schema it actually needs, preserving thousands of context tokens.
GoRoute AI Gateway can ingest any standard OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 REST API specification and automatically project it as an MCP tool server.

The gateway's OpenAPITransport parses operations (paths), extracts input schemas from parameters and requestBody, and synthesizes native MCP tool schemas: type OpenAPIOperation struct { OperationID string `json:"operation_id"` Method string `json:"method"` PathPattern string `json:"path_pattern"` Summary string `json:"summary"` Description string `json:"description"` InputSchema map[string]any `json:"input_schema"` PathParams []string `json:"path_params"` QueryParams []string `json:"query_params"` }

Path Parameter Interpolation: Automatically maps tool arguments to URL path variables (e.g. /v1/users/{userId} $\rightarrow$ substituted with args["userId"]). Query Parameter Mapping: Arguments designated as query parameters are encoded into the URL query string. JSON Request Body Encoding: Body parameters are validated against the OpenAPI schema and posted as application/json. SSRF Hardening: Outbound HTTP calls use the gateway's centralized network.Policy with IP pinning, loopback filtering, and cloud metadata blocking. Arbitrary Decimal Handling: Monetary amounts and high-precision IDs in API responses are preserved using json.Number without IEEE-754 precision loss.

Architecture 50 Tools 200 Tools 500 Tools Traditional Upfront Ingestion ~15,000 tokens ~60,000 tokens Exceeds context limits / ~150,000 tokens Progressive Tool Discovery ~450 tokens (meta-tools + handles) ~500 tokens ~550 tokens Net Token Reduction 97.0% 99.1% 99.6% [!TIP] Use progressive discovery for multi-agent workflows (such as LangChain, AutoGen, or Claude Code) that interact with corporate microservice meshes. The agent retains full visibility into available tools while avoiding token exhaustion.

Local command-line MCP tools (such as CLI database clients, git helpers, file system scanners, and Python analysis scripts) communicate over standard input and output streams (stdin / stdout). Executing untrusted or arbitrary binaries on a production host presents critical security risks: Environment Leakage: Malicious child processes could inspect parent environment variables and exfiltrate database credentials, cloud access keys, or the gateway's AES-256 master keys. Resource Exhaustion: Hung or runaway scripts could consume 100% CPU, leak file descriptors, or flood stdout to exhaust system memory. Arbitrary Code Execution: Attackers attempting command injection could spawn unauthorized shells (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, nc). GoRoute AI Gateway embeds a secure Process Supervisor (internal/mcp/transport_stdio.go) that isolates Stdio tools inside strict execution sandboxes with fail-closed access controls. Isolated Child Process No Yes Gateway Tool Invocation Binary in AllowedBinaries? 403 ErrBinaryNotAllowed(Fail-Closed) Spawn Subprocess Sandbox Parse Line-Delimited JSON-RPC Response Purged EnvironmentPATH, HOME, GOROUTE_SANDBOX=1(Master keys stripped) Context Deadline (30s)(Auto SIGKILL on timeout) Output Buffer Limit (10MB)(io.LimitReader) Background Stderr Drain

The supervisor will refuse to spawn any binary unless it explicitly appears in StdioSecurityPolicy.AllowedBinaries. // StdioSecurityPolicy defines the sandboxing rules for subprocess execution. type StdioSecurityPolicy struct { AllowedBinaries []string `json:"allowed_binaries"` DefaultTimeout time.Duration `json:"default_timeout"` MaxOutputBytes int64 `json:"max_output_bytes"` } The gateway checks both the absolute filesystem path and the executable base name (filepath.Base): func (t *StdioTransport) isBinaryAllowed(binaryPath string) bool { if len(t.policy.AllowedBinaries) == 0 { return false // Fail closed if allowlist is empty } base := filepath.Base(binaryPath) for _, allowed := range t.policy.AllowedBinaries { if allowed == "*" || allowed == binaryPath || allowed == base { return true } } return false } If an unauthorized binary is requested, execution halts immediately with ErrBinaryNotAllowed: mcp: stdio binary is not in approved allowlist: "/bin/sh"

When launching child processes, the gateway completely purges the host process environment. Secrets such as GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY, GATEWAY_MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and GATEWAY_POSTGRES_DSN are never inherited by child processes: // Scrub environment variables: strictly isolate process from gateway secrets cmd.Env = []string{ "PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"), "HOME=" + os.Getenv("HOME"), "LANG=en_US.UTF-8", "GOROUTE_SANDBOX=1", } // Inject only explicitly declared static headers as environment variables for k, v := range server.StaticHeaders { safeKey := strings.ToUpper(strings.ReplaceAll(k, "-", "_")) cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, safeKey+"="+v) }

Default Timeout (30s): Every tool invocation is governed by context.WithTimeout(ctx, policy.DefaultTimeout). If a process hangs, enters an infinite loop, or waits for user input, the supervisor terminates it immediately with SIGKILL. Output Buffer Clamping (10 MB): Stdout streams are bounded via io.LimitReader(stdout, policy.MaxOutputBytes). A runaway process attempting to flood the output buffer is truncated, preventing out-of-memory panics. Background Stderr Diagnostics: Stderr is drained in an independent background goroutine. If a subprocess crashes with a non-zero exit code, its stderr diagnostics are captured in gateway logs to assist operators without polluting JSON-RPC stdout channels.

To enable and configure Stdio execution in your deployment: mcp: enabled: true # Explicitly enable local subprocess execution (defaults to false) allow_stdio_servers: true execution_timeout_seconds: 30 max_payload_bytes: 10485760 # 10 MB # Permitted executable allowlist allowed_binaries: - "/usr/local/bin/git" - "sqlite3" - "node" - "python3"

Register a local CLI tool using the stdio:// URL scheme: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/admin/v1/mcp-servers" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-master-admin-default-key-change-me" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "slug": "local-sqlite", "name": "Local SQLite Query Tool", "transport_type": "stdio", "protocol_version": "2026-07-28", "endpoint_url": "stdio://sqlite3 /data/production.db", "is_active": true, "static_headers": { "SQLITE_ENABLE_JSON1": "1" } }'

documents.t: The gateway's command parser (parseCommandLine) handles quoted arguments and backslash escapes cleanly: stdio://python3 /opt/tools/analyzer.py --mode="read-only" --db="sales report.db"

[!NOTE] In containerized Kubernetes deployments, ensure that any binaries referenced by Stdio servers are pre-installed in the container image or mounted via read-only volumes. [!CAUTION] Never add general-purpose command interpreters (such as bash, sh, zsh, sudo, or eval) to allowed_binaries. Restrict the allowlist strictly to dedicated CLI utilities with known, bounded execution profiles.

GoRoute AI Gateway implements the Linux Foundation Agent-to-Agent (A2A v1.0) protocol specification. It serves as an enterprise gateway for autonomous agent discovery, asynchronous multi-step task delegation, real-time event streaming, and cross-framework agent federation. [!NOTE] All A2A data plane endpoints require standard Bearer token authentication using a tenant Virtual API Key: Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e

Protocol / Method Endpoint Description GET /.well-known/agent-card.json RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized & RFC 7515 JWS signed Agent Card POST /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug} Dual-binding message dispatch (JSON-RPC 2.0 & HTTP+JSON) GET /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks List tasks managed by the agent GET /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID} Inspect state, iteration budget, and outputs for a task POST /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}:cancel Safely abort an in-flight task execution GET /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}:subscribe Subscribe-First SSE stream emitting monotonic a2a-events gRPC lf.a2a.v1.A2AService Native high-performance gRPC service POST /v1/chat/completions (model: "a2a/{slug}") OpenAI-compatible bridge for multi-agent workflows

Exposes the gateway's canonical agent identity formatted with RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) and signed with RFC 7515 JWS (ES256). External agents and registries use this card to verify capabilities, cryptographic public keys, and supported endpoints.
curl http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent-card.json

{ "name": "GoRoute AI Gateway Agent Service", "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Enterprise Autonomous Routing, Aggregation & Inference Agent", "supportedInterfaces": [ { "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/analyst", "protocolBinding": "HTTP+JSON" }, { "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/analyst", "protocolBinding": "JSON-RPC-2.0" }, { "url": "grpc://localhost:9090", "protocolBinding": "gRPC" } ], "capabilities": { "streaming": true, "asyncTasks": true, "pushNotifications": true }, "signatures": [ { "header": { "alg": "ES256", "kid": "gw-a2a-signer-v1", "typ": "JWT" }, "signature": "MEUCIQDx41..." } ] }
Dispatches messages to upstream agents. GoRoute inspects the request body and transparently handles both JSON-RPC 2.0 and HTTP+JSON Protobuf REST formats.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "req-a2a-001", "method": "tasks/send", "params": { "message": { "role": "ROLE_USER", "parts": [ { "text": "Perform portfolio Value-at-Risk assessment for Portfolio Q3." } ] } } }' JSON-RPC 2.0 Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "req-a2a-001", "result": { "role": "ROLE_AGENT", "parts": [ { "text": "Portfolio risk assessment completed: VaR (95% confidence) is 1.42%." } ], "taskId": "task_a2a_5b91a7c0", "state": "completed" } }

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "message": { "role": "ROLE_USER", "parts": [ { "text": "Calculate VaR 99% for portfolio." } ] }, "budget": { "max_cost_micros": 5000000, "max_iterations": 10 } }'
Inspect, list, and control asynchronous agent execution lifecycles.

curl http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "id": "task_a2a_5b91a7c0", "agent_slug": "risk-analyst", "state": "working", "created_at": "2026-11-10T12:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-11-10T12:00:05Z", "iterations_executed": 3, "max_iterations": 10, "cost_incurred_micros": 12500 }

Safely terminates background execution and prevents further upstream model spend: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0:cancel \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e"

Clients connect to stream durable task events (status transitions, intermediate thoughts, artifact publications) in real-time. Emits a2a-event Server-Sent Events with strictly monotonic sequence numbers (seq). curl -N http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0:subscribe \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Accept: text/event-stream"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/event-stream Cache-Control: no-cache Connection: keep-alive event: a2a-event data: {"seq":1,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"working","timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:01Z"} event: a2a-event data: {"seq":2,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"working","thought":"Fetching historical volatility for 50 tickers...","timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:02Z"} event: a2a-event data: {"seq":3,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"completed","output":{"role":"ROLE_AGENT","parts":[{"text":"VaR calculation complete."}]},"timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:05Z"}
For latency-critical agent-to-agent communication, GoRoute exposes a native gRPC server implementing the official Linux Foundation Protobuf contract.

syntax = "proto3"; package lf.a2a.v1; service A2AService { rpc SendMessage(SendMessageRequest) returns (SendMessageResponse); rpc GetTask(GetTaskRequest) returns (Task); rpc ListTasks(ListTasksRequest) returns (ListTasksResponse); rpc CancelTask(CancelTaskRequest) returns (Task); rpc SubscribeToTask(SubscribeToTaskRequest) returns (stream StreamTaskResponse); }

package main import ( "context" "fmt" "google.golang.org/grpc" "google.golang.org/grpc/metadata" pb "github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/internal/a2a/pb" ) func main() { conn, _ := grpc.Dial("localhost:9090", grpc.WithInsecure()) defer conn.Close() client := pb.NewA2AServiceClient(conn) md := metadata.Pairs("authorization", "Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e") ctx := metadata.NewOutgoingContext(context.Background(), md) resp, err := client.SendMessage(ctx, &pb.SendMessageRequest{ AgentSlug: "risk-analyst", Message: &pb.Message{ Role: pb.MessageRole_ROLE_USER, Parts: []*pb.Part{pb.NewTextPart("Run risk audit")}, }, }) if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Printf("Task ID: %s, Response: %v\n", resp.TaskId, resp.Message) }
Allows standard OpenAI Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to orchestrate multi-agent workflows without changing client libraries by specifying model: "a2a/{agent_slug}".

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "a2a/risk-analyst", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Compute Value-at-Risk for Portfolio 4"} ] }' Multi-Turn Resumption (TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED)​ When an upstream agent requires clarifying input, GoRoute returns an assistant response with finish_reason: "stop" containing the agent's question. Callers resume execution simply by sending the next user turn back to model: "a2a/{agent_slug}"; GoRoute automatically reconciles conversational context with the active taskId.

Administrators can instantly disable an agent across all cluster nodes using the control plane API: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/v1/a2a/agents/agent_0192ab/kill-switch \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "killed": true }' When tripped, subsequent invocations immediately fail-closed returning HTTP 503 agent_killed.

GoRoute AI Gateway exposes an OpenAI-compatible data plane supporting 23 primary /v1 paths (26 HTTP operations) across 73 ProviderType profiles (plus CustomOpenAICompatible). All routes execute with sub-2ms gateway overhead, automated circuit breaking, cross-provider fallbacks, and real-time micro-dollar accounting. [!NOTE] All data plane routes accept standard OpenAI SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) and raw HTTP clients. Set your client base_url to http://localhost:8080/v1 and supply a Virtual API Key (sk-gw-...) via the Authorization header.
Every data plane request requires a tenant-scoped Virtual API Key: Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e

Every response returned by GoRoute includes rich tracing, routing, and FinOps telemetry: Header Description Example X-Gateway-Request-Id Unique UUID assigned to the request lifecycle req_991efda4-7fab-4b03 X-Trace-Id W3C / OpenTelemetry distributed trace identifier bad98e7deea34d7c810a963d9ed2c4ef X-Gateway-Provider The winning upstream provider selected for execution gemini, anthropic, openai X-Gateway-Model The physical upstream model that processed the request gemini-2.5-flash, claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 X-Gateway-Cost-Micros Exact micro-dollar spend incurred ($0.000001 USD) 45 ($0.000045 USD) X-Gateway-Routing-Time Gateway Stage 1 + Stage 2 routing overhead 14 µs X-Gateway-Cache Exact-match cache evaluation status HIT or MISS Retry-After Cooldown period sent on HTTP 429 rate limit errors 45 (seconds)

In addition to logical aliases (fast, reasoning), GoRoute allows clients to bypass model groups and target upstream models directly using provider/model syntax (e.g., anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, cerebras/llama-3.3-70b, bedrock/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0, vertex/gemini-2.5-pro): Layer 2 Provider Subscription Check: The caller's organization must have an active subscription for the target provider. Layer 3 Model Policy Check: The requested model must not be disabled by the organization's model availability policy. Tenant Credential Isolation: The organization must have an active credential for the target provider stored in the vault. Host environment variables are never leaked across tenant boundaries. Catalog Provisioning: The gateway may provision model records from its catalog when needed. Catalog contents and discovery behavior depend on the gateway build and configuration; a provider-side model ID is not automatically available to every tenant or key. Fail-Closed Boundary: If repository queries fail or the model is unconfigured/unauthorized, GoRoute fails closed and returns HTTP 404 model_group_not_found (explicit model requests never silently fall back to unrelated tenant model groups).

When stack space is exhausted, the runtime allocates a contiguous block twice the size and copies the existing stack over." }, "finish_reason": "stop" } ], "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 24, "completion_tokens": 42, "total_tokens": 66 } }

GoRoute transparently normalizes requests targeting frontier reasoning models: Reasoning Effort (reasoning_effort: "low" | "medium" | "high"): OpenAI Reasoning (o1, o3, o3-mini): Converts role: "system" to role: "developer", translates max_tokens to max_completion_tokens, and automatically strips unsupported sampling parameters (temperature, top_p). Anthropic Claude: Enables extended thinking with token budgets (1024, 4096, 16384) and omits temperature/top_p as mandated by Anthropic. Google Gemini: Sets thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget for Gemini 2.5 thinking models. Anthropic Role Alternation on Tools: When returning multiple parallel tool outputs (role: "tool"), GoRoute automatically consolidates consecutive tool results into a single user message with multiple tool_result content blocks to satisfy Anthropic's strict alternating turn protocol.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-4o", "input": "Summarize quantum computing principles", "instructions": "Be concise, use bullet points", "stream": true }'

Emits Responses events (response.created, response.output_item.added, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done, response.output_item.done, response.completed, response.done): event: response.created data: {"response":{"id":"resp_0192a","status":"in_progress","model":"gpt-4o"}} event: response.output_text.delta data: {"output_index":0,"delta":"Quantum computing utilizes superposition and entanglement."} event: response.completed data: {"response":{"id":"resp_0192a","status":"completed"}} event: response.done data: {}

GoRoute AI Gateway implements the official MCP 2026-07-28 stateless Streamable HTTP specification with backward compatibility for MCP 2025-11-25. It functions as an enterprise Virtual Hub aggregating distributed tool servers, validating schemas, enforcing Virtual Key scopes, and eliminating prompt token overhead with progressive discovery. [!NOTE] All MCP routes authenticate using the standard Bearer header with a tenant-scoped Virtual API Key: Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e

Protocol Method Route Description POST /mcp Virtual Hub multi-server aggregator (tools/list, tools/call) POST /mcp/{serverSlug} Scoped execution targeted at a single upstream MCP server POST /mcp/toolsets/{toolsetSlug} Execution routed through a curated, vetted toolset GET /mcp/subscriptions/listen Client SSE stream for dynamic catalog invalidation events GET /mcp-rest/tools/list Plain REST list of aggregated tools without JSON-RPC framing POST /mcp-rest/tools/call Plain REST tool execution with direct JSON payloads GET /v1/goroute/mcp/registry Progressive discovery feed issuing 256-bit tool handles

Aggregates all registered, active, and tenant-authorized MCP servers into a single unified JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint. Tool names are automatically namespaced (<server-slug>__<tool-name>) to prevent collisions.
Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json, text/event-stream Origin: http://localhost:8080 Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }' Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "tools": [ { "name": "github__create_issue", "description": "Create an issue in a GitHub repository", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "owner": { "type": "string" }, "repo": { "type": "string" }, "title": { "type": "string" }, "body": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["owner", "repo", "title"] } }, { "name": "fin_tools__calculate_dcf", "description": "Calculate discounted cash flow with high precision", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "discount_rate": { "type": "number" }, "cash_flows": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "number" } } }, "required": ["discount_rate", "cash_flows"] } } ], "_meta": { "goroute.ai/server_outcomes": { "github": "success", "fin-tools": "success" } } } }

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "github__create_issue", "arguments": { "owner": "goroute-ai", "repo": "ai-gateway-go", "title": "Bug: fix connection pooling", "body": "Detailed description of the issue." } } }' Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Issue #42 created successfully at https://github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/issues/42" } ], "isError": false } }

Routes JSON-RPC 2.0 requests exclusively to the upstream server matching {serverSlug}. Tool names do not require namespace prefixes in scoped mode. GoRoute preserves arbitrary decimal precision for financial and scientific tools using Go's big.Rat and json.Number without IEEE-754 floating point distortion. curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/fin-tools \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 10, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "calculate_dcf", "arguments": { "discount_rate": 0.08251294819284719, "cash_flows": [1000000, 1500000, 2000000] } } }' Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 10, "result": { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Net Present Value: 3824192.48291048192" } ], "isError": false } }

Executes tool calls through a predefined, vetted subset of pinned tools spanning multiple backend servers. Useful for creating role-restricted environments (e.g. read-only-analyst, devops-tier-1). curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/toolsets/analyst-tools \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 20, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }'
Standard RESTful endpoints designed for traditional HTTP clients, SDKs, and webhooks that interact without JSON-RPC 2.0 framing.

Query Parameters​ server_slug (optional): Filter tools registered under a specific upstream server. curl "http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/list?server_slug=fin-tools" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "tools": [ { "id": "tool_019248ab-3c4d-5e6f", "server_id": "mcp_srv_771829a", "server_slug": "fin-tools", "name": "calculate_dcf", "description": "Calculate discounted cash flow with high precision", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "discount_rate": { "type": "number" }, "cash_flows": { "type": "array" } }, "required": ["discount_rate", "cash_flows"] }, "cost_per_call_micros": 500, "is_active": true } ] }

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/call \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "server_slug": "fin-tools", "tool_name": "calculate_dcf", "arguments": { "discount_rate": 0.08, "cash_flows": [500000, 750000, 1000000] } }' Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Net Present Value: 1851240.22" } ], "is_error": false } Error Handling​ HTTP 400 AmbiguousToolName: Returned when tool_name matches multiple active servers and server_slug was omitted. Contains a matching_servers array. HTTP 403 mcp_server_forbidden: Caller's Virtual API Key is not authorized for the requested server or toolset.
To prevent token exhaustion when exposing hundreds of tools to LLM agent loops, GoRoute issues compact 256-bit cryptographic tool handles (tool_hdl_<64 hex chars>).

curl http://localhost:8080/v1/goroute/mcp/registry \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" Response (HTTP 200 OK)​ { "servers": [ { "server_slug": "fin-tools", "tools": [ { "name": "calculate_dcf", "description": "Calculates discounted cash flow valuation", "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0" } ] } ] }

When progressive discovery is active in an agent loop, models only receive tool handles and descriptions. When a model decides to invoke a tool, it calls built-in meta-tools: search_tools: Keyword search over registered tool definitions: { "query": "discounted cash flow", "limit": 5 } get_tool_schema: Resolves full JSON Schema by handle: { "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0" } Execution via Handle: Directly call POST /mcp-rest/tools/call using tool_name: "tool_hdl_...". If an upstream schema mutates, stale handles fail-closed with HTTP 404/410.

[!NOTE] This guide is for contributors developing the ai-gateway-go repository itself. If you want to route Claude Code or IDE traffic through a running GoRoute AI Gateway instance, see Claude Code Integration and Cursor, Continue & Cline. GoRoute AI Gateway (goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go) is engineered from the ground up to be maintainable, verifiable, and extensible by both human software engineers and autonomous AI coding agents (such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Google Antigravity). To guarantee that agent-generated pull requests maintain architectural invariants, code quality, and security boundaries, the codebase incorporates a hierarchical context architecture consisting of: Root CLAUDE.md: Compact project instructions and essential commands (under 100 lines). Modular .claude/rules/: Scoped sub-domain guidelines (go-backend.md, frontend-web.md, api-contracts.md). Universal AGENTS.md: Portable repository guidance for all autonomous agent engines. Deterministic Verification Loops: Non-interactive commands to validate syntax, typing, static analysis, race conditions, contracts, and frontend bundle budgets.

The root CLAUDE.md file serves as the immediate instruction entrypoint for Claude Code sessions. To ensure high token efficiency, it is maintained under a strict 100-line limit while establishing the 7 core repository invariants: CLAUDE.md: Under 100 Lines(Immediate Context) 1. Micro-Dollar FinOps (Integer Arithmetic) 2. SSRF & Egress Protection (internal/security/network) 3. Fail-Closed 4-Layer RBAC (Org/Team/User/Key) 4. AES-256-GCM Credential Vault 5. Contract-Guided Specs (OpenAPI 3.1 & Protos) 6. Single-Binary Embedded UI (Under 400 KB Budget) 7. Immutable Model Pricing Audit History

Integer Micro-Dollar FinOps: All financial and spend calculations must use 64-bit integer micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000 micro-dollars) with intermediate pico-dollar precision. Never use floating-point types (float32 / float64) for money. SSRF & Outbound Egress Protection: Outbound network requests must use internal/security/network safe HTTP transport (SafeTransport, DialContext). Never use raw unvalidated http.DefaultClient or unpinned IPs for provider egress. Fail-Closed RBAC & Auth: Multi-tenant authorization (internal/auth/rbac.go) is strictly fail-closed across all 4 tiers (Organization → Team → User → Virtual Key). Credential Vault: Upstream provider API keys and secrets must remain encrypted via AES-256-GCM (internal/storage/vault.go) at rest and in transit. Contract-Guided Architecture: API and wire contracts are defined in docs/openapi/gateway.openapi.yaml, docs/specs/mcp/, and docs/specs/a2a/. Verify contracts with go run ./cmd/specgen. Single-Binary Web UI Embedding: The Operator UI in web/ compiles into internal/ui/dist/ and is embedded via Go embed.FS (//go:embed all:dist). Total frontend bundle size must strictly respect budget constraints (under 400 KB total; verified via web/scripts/check-budget.mjs). Immutable Pricing History: Model pricing updates must append an immutable audit record to model_pricing_history.

Rather than crowding the root prompt with domain-specific rules, the repository utilizes modular rule definitions located in .claude/rules/. AI agents activate these instructions dynamically based on the files they touch.

Located at .claude/rules/go-backend.md, this guide enforces Go idioms and safety standards: Strict Dependency Direction: Package dependencies point strictly inward toward domain definitions in internal/domain: cmd/: Application entrypoints (cmd/gateway, cmd/specgen, cmd/catalog-sync). pkg/: Public, stable, embeddable SDKs (pkg/gateway). internal/: Private implementation packages (internal/server, internal/router, internal/adapter, etc.). internal/domain/: Foundational domain types, interfaces, request/response models, and error codes. Chi Router Conventions: Handlers follow standard http.HandlerFunc signatures: func (s *GatewayServer) handleX(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request). Path parameters extracted via chi.URLParam(r, "paramName"). Query parameters extracted via r.URL.Query().Get("key"). JSON serialization via writeJSON(w, statusCode, data). Unified error serialization via domain.WriteHTTPError(w, err). Zero-Allocation Hot Path: Hot inference routes (POST /v1/chat/completions) must avoid unnecessary heap allocations, redundant JSON reflection, or blocking synchronous database writes. Safe Network Egress: Direct instantiation of &http.Client{} is prohibited. All outbound requests must use network.NewSafeTransport with DNS pinning, private IP filtering, and link-local address blocking.

Located at .claude/rules/frontend-web.md, this guide establishes rules for modifying the Operator Web UI: Technology Stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS v3 (dark mode enabled via slate/zinc palette). Icon Imports: Use lucide-react with tree-shaking named imports (e.g. import { Activity, Shield } from 'lucide-react'). Avoid importing the entire library to prevent bundle bloat. Bundle Budget Verification: Every pull request modifying web/ must pass check-budget.mjs with uncompressed size under 380 KB and gzip under 110 KB. Distribution Synchronization: When frontend source files are changed, make ui-build must be executed to rebuild the bundle and sync artifacts to internal/ui/dist/ before committing.

Located at .claude/rules/api-contracts.md, this rule governs wire formats and backwards compatibility: Authoritative Contract Files: Gateway OpenAPI: docs/openapi/gateway.openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.1.0). MCP OpenAPI & Schema: docs/openapi/mcp.openapi.yaml and docs/specs/mcp/2026-07-28/schema.json. A2A OpenAPI & Protobuf: docs/openapi/a2a.openapi.yaml and docs/specs/a2a/v1.0/a2a.proto. Validation Utility: Agents must execute go run ./cmd/specgen to ensure that route schemas, protobuf definitions, and documentation match the Go code. Attribution Headers: Responses must include standard attribution telemetry (X-Gateway-Request-Id, X-Gateway-Provider, X-Gateway-Model, X-Gateway-Cost-Micros, X-Gateway-Routing-Time, X-Gateway-Cache).

AGENTS.md is the cross-engine specification file designed for tools like Cursor, Copilot Workspace, Antigravity, and autonomous agent loops. It emphasizes: Codebase Mapping: Directs agents to read docs/CODEBASE_MAP.md before exploring code. Change Expectations: Agents must state the exact commands executed and tests run in their change summaries. Preservation of Unrelated Work: Agents must not revert, rewrite, or touch unrelated code or user changes. Self-Correction Strategy: When a test fails or go vet produces warnings, agents must inspect the failure, apply the minimal targeted fix, and rerun the test suite rather than disabling tests.

Autonomous agents must execute the deterministic verification pipeline before declaring any task complete. The commands below are fast, reproducible, and runnable locally or in CI: Step Verification Goal Command Success Criteria 1. Formatting Check Go code formatting gofmt -l . Output must be empty (0 files listed). 2. Static Analysis Go type and idiom validation go vet ./... Exits with return code 0; zero warnings. 3. API Specs Validate OpenAPI & Protobuf contracts go run ./cmd/specgen Passes contract validation without errors. 4. Unit Tests Concurrent race detection go test -race -count=1 ./internal/... ./pkg/... All package unit tests pass under Go race detector. 5. Focused Test Rapid feedback during edits go test -v -race -run <TestName> ./internal/<pkg>/... Specified unit test passes cleanly. 6. Frontend Build Build UI & verify bundle budget make ui-build Passes Vite build and check-budget.mjs threshold. 7. UI Dist Sync Confirm embedded dist is mirrored make ui-check-dist git status shows zero uncommitted diffs in internal/ui/dist. 8. Binary Build Compile production executable go build ./cmd/gateway Produces executable binary gateway. 9. Full Check Comprehensive pre-flight check make release-check All verification checks pass end-to-end.

Agents can run this one-line verification recipe to confirm entire repository integrity: gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./internal/server ./internal/router ./internal/auth && go build ./cmd/gateway [!TIP] When testing data plane changes without running live upstream providers, use the built-in mock provider adapter (internal/adapter/mock.go) or the lightweight local test server (configs/config.yaml) to achieve 100% deterministic test coverage without network dependencies.

GoRoute AI Gateway supports a layered configuration architecture: Built-in Defaults: Hardcoded, zero-dependency defaults optimized for instant developer startup. Declarative YAML (configs/config.yaml): Structured configuration defining storage backends, security boundaries, rate limits, model groups, and routing topologies. Environment Variable Overrides (GATEWAY_* / os.environ/VAR): Production overrides for Kubernetes ConfigMaps, container runtime secrets, and 12-factor cloud deployments. Go SDK Options (pkg/gateway): In-process configuration primitives for embedded architectures.

Set your upstream provider API keys directly in your shell or container definition. The gateway automatically spins up an in-memory repository, provisions an AES-256-GCM vault, and configures default model aliases: # Frontier LLM Providers export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..." export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..." export MISTRAL_API_KEY="mis_..." # Enterprise Cloud Hyperscalers export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="AKIA..." export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="..." export AWS_REGION="us-east-1" export GCP_PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project" export GCP_REGION="us-central1" # Gateway Master Secrets export GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY="sk-gw-master-secret-passphrase-change-me" export GATEWAY_MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY="0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" # Launch Gateway ./ai-gateway

Supply the path to your YAML configuration file via the -config CLI argument: ./ai-gateway -config /etc/goroute/config.yaml The gateway resolves environment variable secret placeholders matching os.environ/VARIABLE_NAME inside strings dynamically during YAML parsing: model_params: model: "openai/gpt-4o" api_key: "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"
