Use the provider's current model documentation to choose an ID, then check the gateway's tenant-filtered GET /v1/models inventory with the same virtual key your application will use. That inventory is the reference for models currently exposed to that caller. Provider access, gateway catalog discovery/sync settings, organization policies, and key allowlists can all affect availability. A model listed by a provider is not by itself confirmation that a particular GoRoute deployment can route it. When catalog discovery is enabled, the gateway can synchronize models exposed by supported providers. Discovery does not make every provider model universally available: provider credentials, adapter/protocol compatibility, organization policy, and virtual-key permissions still apply. See Model Management & Access Control and model catalog configuration.
documents.s: Find model IDs available to your key

documents.t: GoRoute embeds a curated catalog of 4,627 models (internal/modelcatalog/catalog.json.gz) with operation-level support and modality pricing provenance. When a model is not yet in the catalog or has CapabilityUnknown fields, internal/modelcatalog/generalizations.go (InferFamilyCapabilities, BackfillCapabilities, StripRegionalModelPrefix) supplies explicit heuristic defaults (Inferred: true, Source: "family-pattern-heuristic") for context windows and capabilities (tools, streaming, vision, reasoning, structured outputs) without treating unverified catalog rates as verified for budgeted traffic.

In v1.6.0, checkDeploymentOperation (internal/router/reliability.go) enforces operation compatibility before dispatching a request: Adapter-level check: Adapters implementing OperationSupportChecker.SupportsOperation(op) reject unsupported operations with HTTP 501 Not Implemented (<op>_not_supported). Model-level check: When GlobalModel.SupportedOperations is populated, requests for operations outside that allowlist are rejected with HTTP 400 Bad Request (unsupported_operation).

GoRoute abstracts vendor authentication into four distinct automated mechanisms: Standard Bearer Authentication (BearerAuthStrategy): Injects Authorization: Bearer <token> automatically for 35+ providers. Cryptographic AWS SigV4 (SigV4Signer): Signs requests dynamically using IAM access keys, temporary session tokens, and regional HMAC-SHA256 calculations. Google OAuth2 Assertion Exchange (TokenSource): Signs RS256 JWT assertions with GCP Service Account private keys, exchanges them for access tokens with oauth2.googleapis.com, and handles background caching. Microsoft Entra ID & API Key (AzureAuthStrategy): Automatically distinguishes between standard Azure resource keys (api-key: <key>) and Entra ID tokens (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
Configure providers in configs/config.yaml using either explicit provider prefixes or virtual alias routing:

Call upstream providers directly by prefixing the model parameter: # Routes directly to Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer your-virtual-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "cerebras/llama3.3-70b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}' # Routes directly to Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer your-virtual-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'

Define resilient model aliases in configs/config.yaml: model_list: # Fast Tier: Gemini 2.5 Flash with fallback to GPT-4o-mini - model_name: fast routing_strategy: weighted-shuffle fallbacks: ["fast-backup"] model_params: model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY weight: 100 - model_name: fast-backup model_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY # Reasoning Tier: Anthropic Claude Sonnet with fallback to Azure GPT-4o - model_name: reasoning routing_strategy: least-busy fallbacks: ["azure-gpt4o"] model_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: azure-gpt4o model_params: model: azure/gpt-4o api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: "https://my-enterprise.openai.azure.com" azure_deployment_name: "gpt-4o-prod" api_version: "2024-08-01-preview"

Every request processed across any of the 73 ProviderType profiles includes standardized audit and FinOps telemetry headers: Header Description Example X-Gateway-Request-Id Unique UUID assigned to the client invocation req_01h8a... X-Trace-Id Distributed W3C trace ID for end-to-end tracing 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 X-Gateway-Provider The actual upstream provider that fulfilled the request bedrock, cerebras, openai X-Gateway-Model The upstream foundation model executed anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5 X-Gateway-Cost-Micros Exact cost of the invocation in micro-dollars ($1 = 1,000,000 µ$) 1250 ($0.001250) X-Gateway-Routing-Time Gateway latency overhead before upstream dispatch 4.2ms X-Gateway-Cache Cache hit status (HIT or MISS) HIT Retry-After Cooldown period emitted during upstream 429 rate limit events 60
GoRoute AI Gateway follows Semantic Versioning and Keep a Changelog. Each release includes automated SQL schema migrations, OpenAPI contract validation, and multi-replica Kubernetes verification.

Version Release Date Highlights v1.7.0 2026-11-14 SSRF & media fetch hardening, pure-SDK parity (ConnectRealtime, WithHTTPClient), 63-path specgen parity, round-robin routing, Helm chart (0.2.0), and migrations 0013–0015. v1.6.0 2026-11-13 Maximum provider & model compatibility, modality FinOps, 0012 migration, hardened Kustomize manifests (deployments/k8s/), and containerized production test suite. v1.5.0 2026-11-13 Operator RBAC & inbound JWT/OIDC, Redis Cluster/Sentinel support, durable spend outbox, shared circuit breakers, streaming guardrail redaction, and OTLP tracing.

Before upgrading across minor versions: Check the target release notes for any new required environment variables or production validation rules (for example, v1.5.0 introduced GATEWAY_ENV=production default-secret rejection and disabled master-key data-plane fallback). Review configs/config.example.yaml for newly added configuration blocks.

GoRoute embeds all PostgreSQL migrations (migrations/0001_*.sql through 0015_*.sql) directly in the gateway binary and applies pending up-migrations atomically at startup (or via -migrate-only / the Helm migration pre-upgrade hook job). For zero-downtime rolling upgrades in Kubernetes: Ensure your PostgreSQL user has DDL permissions (CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX) or run a pre-upgrade migration job. Take a PostgreSQL snapshot before applying major schema changes (such as 0008 spend outbox, 0012 cache-write and operations columns, or 0013–0015 user/team/org concurrency and budget limits). Upgrade the gateway image tag and monitor /readyz before draining old pods: kubectl -n goroute-prod set image deployment/gateway gateway=ghcr.io/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go:v1.7.0 kubectl -n goroute-prod rollout status deployment/gateway --timeout=120s
After rollout completes: Confirm GET /healthz and GET /readyz return 200 OK. Run make test-canary against a staging environment to validate live provider routing and modality endpoints.
Release Date: 2026-11-13 Theme: Enterprise Security Hardening, Redis Cluster Support, Durable FinOps, Streaming Guardrails & API Parity

Operator RBAC & Inbound JWT/OIDC (internal/auth/, internal/server/handlers_admin.go): Added role-based operator authorization (platform_admin, org_admin, org_viewer) with organization-scoped control-plane enforcement, inbound JWT/OIDC verification, and disabled master-key data-plane fallback. Fail-Closed Team Lookup & Allowlist Persistence (internal/storage/postgres.go): Enforced fail-closed team lookup error handling and persisted all team allowlists (allowed_models, allowed_mcp_servers, allowed_a2a_agents, allowed_client_apps) in PostgreSQL. HTTP Security Headers & CORS Middleware (internal/server/security_headers.go): Added SecurityHeadersMiddleware (HSTS opt-in via server.enable_hsts, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Content-Security-Policy) and safe-by-default CORSMiddleware (server.cors_allowed_origins, server.cors_allow_credentials). Per-Organization File Storage Quota & Upload Concurrency Limits (internal/server/handlers_files.go): Added server.max_file_storage_bytes_per_org (default 5 GiB, GATEWAY_MAX_FILE_STORAGE_BYTES_PER_ORG) and server.max_concurrent_file_uploads (default 8, GATEWAY_MAX_CONCURRENT_FILE_UPLOADS) with atomic in-flight reservation tracking (413 storage_quota_exceeded), bounded upload semaphore (429 upload_concurrency_limit), and explicit MultipartForm.RemoveAll() temporary spill-file cleanup. Production Environment Hardening (internal/config/config.go): Updated Config.Validate() to treat both ENV=production and GATEWAY_ENV=production as production signals and reject default admin, encryption, or JWT secrets. Credential & Key Hygiene: Restricted query-string credentials strictly to WebSocket upgrades (/v1/realtime), enforced expiry and revocation on cached virtual keys, and updated golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0. CI & Supply-Chain Security: Pinned all GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml) to immutable 40-character commit SHAs, added .github/workflows/codeql.yml for Go and JavaScript/TypeScript analysis, and added .gitleaks.toml.

Durable Spend Event Outbox (migrations/0008_add_spend_event_outbox.up.sql): Added PostgreSQL spend event outbox with retryable delivery and idempotent Redis spend reconciliation keyed by event ID (gw:spend:applied:{org}). Upper-Bound Budget Reservations & Lease Renewal (internal/finops/, internal/ratelimit/): Added pre-dispatch upper-bound budget reservation with automatic lease renewal for long-running/streaming requests and unified modality budget gating. Budget Reset Period Advancement & PG/Redis Sync (migrations/0011_budget_reset_outbox.up.sql): Fixed PostgresRepository.ResetExpiredBudgetsWithIDs, synchronized entity spent_micros, and cleared Redis spend counters on period rollover. Unpriced Usage & Modality Estimates: Surfaced unpriced_requests and unpriced_tokens in spend summaries instead of silently recording zero cost, and improved preflight token estimates for modality requests.

Redis Cluster & Sentinel Support (internal/storage/, internal/cache/): Upgraded RedisFabric to go-redis UniversalClient (storage.redis_addrs, storage.redis_master_name) with {org:<id>} hash-tagged Lua keys across rate limiting and response caching. Embeddings Reliability & Shared Circuit Breakers (internal/router/): Wired ExecuteEmbeddings through ReliabilityManager retries/fallbacks, shared circuit-breaker failure counts and half-open probe leases in Redis across replicas, and fixed adaptive routing signals and least-busy reservation tracking. Bounded Fallback Traversal & Streaming Retries: Added cycle and depth limits to fallback group traversal and exponential backoff for streaming retries before first output token.

All-Role Scanning, Streaming Redaction & logging_only Mode (internal/guardrails/stream_filter.go, migrations/0010_guardrail_mode.up.sql): Expanded input scanning to all message roles, added output blocking and streaming chunk inspection/redaction, and added logging_only guardrail policy mode. Fail-Closed Policy & Full Inference Coverage: Enforced fail-closed guardrail policy lookups, added provider-neutral scanner hooks, and extended guardrail evaluation across all supported inference endpoints. A2A & MCP Hardening (internal/a2a/, internal/mcp/): Closed the A2A OpenAI bridge bypass, wired inbound/outbound A2A guardrails (RouterService.SetGuardrails), hardened MCP guardrail evaluation, and wired the native A2A gRPC server behind server.grpc_port (GATEWAY_GRPC_PORT).

OpenAI & Anthropic Wire Fidelity (internal/adapter/): Added forwarding for extra_body and unknown top-level parameters (ExtraParams), Anthropic-formatted error envelopes on /v1/messages, streaming TTS (/v1/audio/speech), and tools forwarding on /v1/responses. Canonical Response Cache Keys & Shared Invalidation (internal/cache/): Keyed response cache entries by full canonical output-affecting request fields and propagated cache invalidation epochs across replicas via Redis.

OTLP Distributed Tracing & Uniform Reservoir Sampling (internal/observability/): Added optional OTLP/HTTP distributed tracing (tracing.otlp_endpoint, gen_ai.* span attributes) routed through the outbound SSRF policy, and replaced rolling-overwrite latency histograms with Vitter Algorithm R uniform reservoir sampling. Structured Log Scrubbing & Protected Metrics (internal/logger/): Added logger.ScrubSecrets to mask credentials in structured logs, protected /metrics with admin bearer authentication, and bounded Prometheus label cardinality. Operator Web UI Hardening (web/, internal/ui/): Repaired JSON field bindings, cleared React Query cache on Control Plane lock, self-hosted fonts (zero external font CDN calls), decoupled Playground/Agentic secrets, added GET /admin/v1/mcp/tools, and enforced CI internal/ui/dist parity.
Release Date: 2026-11-13 Theme: Maximum Provider & Model Compatibility, Modality FinOps, Production Test Suite & K8s Hardening

Upstream Catalog Parity & Capability Generalizations (cmd/catalog-sync/, internal/modelcatalog/): Expanded cmd/catalog-sync and internal/modelcatalog with operation-level model support, modality pricing provenance, and explicit inferred capability generalizations (internal/modelcatalog/generalizations.go) without treating unverified catalog rates as verified for budgeted traffic. Operation-Level Routing Enforcement & Certified OpenAI-Compatible Profiles (internal/router/, internal/adapter/openaicompat/): Added SupportedOperations enforcement across router dispatch (internal/router/reliability.go) and expanded certified provider profiles (internal/adapter/openaicompat/extended_profiles.go, validator.go). Multimodal Native Adapter & Responses API Extensions (internal/adapter/): Expanded multimodal content, tool-only streaming, and audio/image/rerank wire handling across native adapters (anthropic, bedrock, cohere, gemini, mistral, ollama, openai, vertex) and /v1/responses.
documents.s: Model Catalog, Provider Compatibility & Operation Enforcement

documents.t: Migration 0012 & Modality Persistence (migrations/): Added migrations/0012_add_cache_write_and_operations.{up,down}.sql for cache-write pricing and per-model operation declarations across PostgreSQL and in-memory repositories. PostgreSQL file_uploads Query Fix (internal/storage/postgres.go): Removed invalid ::uuid casts on VARCHAR(64) org_id, team_id, and user_id columns in CreateFile, GetFile, ListFiles, and DeleteFile. In-Memory Spend Outbox & Redis Breaker Fixes (internal/storage/, internal/cache/): Deleted delivered entries from MemoryRepository.spendOutbox in MarkSpendEventDelivered to prevent $O(N^2)$ lock scans under sustained soak load, and treated redis.Nil cache misses as non-failures in RedisFabric circuit breakers.

Hardened Kubernetes Kustomize Manifests (deployments/k8s/): Added deployments/k8s/ with a 2-replica gateway deployment, non-root securityContext (runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65532, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]), /readyz + /healthz probes, and postgres + redis services. See Kubernetes & Kustomize Deployment. Containerized Production Suite & Load/Canary Harnesses (deployments/, tests/): Added deployments/docker-compose.test.yml, tests/load/ (5-minute Go soak + k6_gateway_smoke.js), tests/canary/ (//go:build canary), tests/e2e/budget_concurrency_test.go, tests/e2e/modality_compat_test.go, tests/e2e/security_boundaries_test.go, and make test-prod-containers (gitleaks, trivy, govulncheck, k6, pgbench, redis-benchmark).
Release Date: 2026-11-14 Theme: Security & SSRF Remediations, Pure-SDK Parity, Operator Web UI Wiring, Helm Chart & Automated Release Packaging

Canonical Provider BaseURL & Preflight SSRF Enforcement (internal/adapter/, internal/server/): Added canonical ValidateAndResolveBaseURL across native adapters (openai, anthropic, mistral, ollama, gemini, azure), openaicompat profiles (ProfileRegistry + resolveEndpointBase), and admin credential creation/rotation/validation handlers. Restricted private-network preflight probes to platform_admin, and hardened Gemini isVertexExpressKey to parsed hostname equality. Isolated Untrusted Media Fetch Policy (internal/adapter/media.go): Added DefaultPublicMediaPolicy and FetchRemoteDataURIWithPolicy, isolating end-user image_url and document.url fetches on ollama and vertex behind strict public-HTTPS mediaPolicy / mediaClient instances (AllowPrivateNetworks: false, AllowInsecureHTTP: false). Response, Header & Concurrency Hardening (internal/server/, internal/auth/, internal/logger/): Emitted strict Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none' on non-UI routes, validated /v1/audio/speech Content-Type, sanitized X-Request-Id and fallback Content-Type, scoped sha256.Sum256 JWT signature checks strictly to RS256/ES256, warned on short auth.default_virtual_key (< 32 chars), streamed multipart image uploads via io.Copy, and fixed a response-marshal race in handleCreateBatch.

WebSocket Realtime & Pure-SDK Modality Wrappers (pkg/gateway/): Added ConnectRealtime (*RealtimeSession with SendEvent, ReadEvent, and Close), WithHTTPClient, and zero-internal-import typed SDK methods (CreateEmbedding, CreateRerank, CreateModeration, CreateResponse, StreamResponse, CreateImage, CreateSpeech, TranscribeAudio, and GetSpendSummary). See the Go SDK API Reference. /v1 + /admin/v1 Spec Parity & Streaming Headers (cmd/specgen/, internal/server/): Updated cmd/specgen to verify both /v1 and /admin/v1 route parity (63 Unified OpenAPI paths), emitted X-Gateway-Provider and X-Gateway-Model before the first SSE chunk on streaming chat completions, and exposed X-Gateway-* telemetry headers via CORS Access-Control-Expose-Headers. Multi-Replica HA & Tri-State Serialization (internal/auth/, internal/storage/, internal/server/): Preserved 3-state allowlists (null = Inherit vs [] = Deny All) across Redis L2 IdentityContext, Team/VirtualKey JSON responses, and optionalStringSlice patch decoding (PATCH/PUT handlers), and ensured PostgresRepository mutations and TEXT[] NOT NULL bindings stay coherent across multi-replica pods.

6th Load-Balancing Strategy (round-robin) (internal/domain/, internal/router/): Added domain.StrategyRoundRobin ("round-robin") with per-ModelGroupID atomic rotation in LoadBalancer.selectRoundRobin. See Routing & Load Balancing. Control-Plane Contract Alignment: Synced TypeScript models and views with spent_micros, 7 user/key roles (platform_admin through service_account / viewer), explicit 3-state Inherit | Deny All | Custom List allowlist controls, round-robin routing strategy, Pricing History modal, full Guardrails controls (mode, scan_all_roles, toxicity filter, content categories), MCPTool.input_schema, OAuth2/static_headers MCP config, none | static | vault_jwt A2A auth, inline valid: false credential validation errors, URL-encoded admin queries, and <ScopedRoleNotice> 403 handling across all 16 sanitizeRuntimeConfig sections. SSE Playground & Nested SPA Assets: Fixed SSE event: error detection and EOF decoder flushing, dynamically populated Playground model aliases from unlocked admin endpoints, removed empty assistant error placeholders, and switched favicon/logo assets to /ui/* paths within the <= 420 KB / <= 125 KB gzip bundle budget.

Migration 0013_user_limits_and_spend_indexes: Adds per-user rpm_limit, tpm_limit, max_concurrent_requests, max_budget_micros, spent_micros, budget_reset_period, and budget_reset_at columns to users, plus (org_id, team_id) and (org_id, user_id) indexes on spend_logs. Migration 0014_budget_reset_outbox_user_scope: Expands budget_reset_outbox_scope_check to CHECK (scope IN ('org', 'team', 'user', 'key')). Migration 0015_team_org_concurrency: Adds max_concurrent_requests to organizations and teams. Helm Chart & Automated Release Packaging (deployments/helm/goroute/, .github/workflows/release.yml, Makefile): Added make release-assets for cross-platform archives (darwin/linux/windows, amd64/arm64), checksums.txt, Helm .tgz (goroute chart 0.2.0 / appVersion: 1.7.0), and Kubernetes bundle archives alongside multi-arch ghcr.io/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go publishing with full OCI image labels. See Helm Chart Deployment.

The SDK exposes Chat for a single user prompt, ChatWithMessages for structured history, and StreamChat for receiving text deltas through a callback. The examples below are function-body snippets and assume ctx context.Context, an initialized gw, and the standard imports.

result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Draft a short status update.", gateway.WithSystem("You are a concise engineering assistant."), gateway.WithTemperature(0.4), gateway.WithMaxTokens(256), ) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println(result.Content) Available request options are WithSystem, WithTemperature, WithMaxTokens, and WithReasoningEffort. The upstream provider determines which options it supports.

result, err := gw.ChatWithMessages(ctx, gateway.ChatRequest{ Model: "fast", Messages: []gateway.Message{ {Role: "system", Content: "You are a concise site reliability engineer."}, {Role: "user", Content: "What should I check first after an HTTP 504?"}, {Role: "assistant", Content: "Check the gateway, upstream health, and timeout logs."}, {Role: "user", Content: "How can I narrow it down?"}, }, }) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println(result.Content)

StreamChat calls onDelta as text arrives from the upstream stream. The callback can return an error to stop processing. result, err := gw.StreamChat(ctx, "fast", "Write a short haiku about Go.", func(delta string) error { _, err := fmt.Print(delta) return err }) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Printf("\nCost: %d µ$\n", result.CostMicros) The gateway translates supported provider streaming responses into the SDK callback. Delivery timing and available content depend on the selected provider; no fixed latency or buffering guarantee is implied.

Pass a context with a timeout to bound the request and cancel work when the caller no longer needs the response: requestCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second) defer cancel() result, err := gw.Chat(requestCtx, "fast", "Summarize this report.") if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println(result.Content)

In v1.7.0, pkg/gateway provides self-contained public request and response structs (zero internal/ package imports) for embeddings, reranking, moderation, the OpenAI Responses API, images, audio, and tokenization: // Vector embeddings emb, err := gw.CreateEmbedding(ctx, gateway.EmbeddingRequest{ Model: "text-embedding-3-small", Input: []string{"GoRoute AI Gateway"}, }) // Document reranking reranked, err := gw.CreateRerank(ctx, gateway.RerankRequest{ Model: "rerank-v3.5", Query: "zero-allocation Go proxy", Documents: []any{"GoRoute routes inference in pure Go."}, }) // OpenAI Responses API (sync or streaming) resp, err := gw.CreateResponse(ctx, gateway.ResponseRequest{ Model: "fast", Input: "Summarize this diff in two bullets.", }) _, err = gw.StreamResponse(ctx, gateway.ResponseRequest{ Model: "fast", Input: "Stream a haiku about Go.", }, func(delta string) error { _, err := fmt.Print(delta) return err }) Additional pure-SDK modality methods include CreateModeration, CreateImage, ImageEdit, ImageVariation, CreateSpeech, TranscribeAudio, Tokenize, CountTokens, and stateful file/batch helpers (UploadFile, ListFiles, GetFile, GetFileContent, DeleteFile, CreateBatch, ListBatches, GetBatch, CancelBatch).

Use ConnectRealtime to open a full-duplex WebSocket session to /v1/realtime using *gateway.RealtimeSession: session, err := gw.ConnectRealtime(ctx, "gpt-4o-realtime-preview") if err != nil { return err } defer session.Close() if err := session.SendEvent(ctx, gateway.RealtimeEvent{ Type: "response.create", }); err != nil { return err } ev, err := session.ReadEvent(ctx) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println("Received event:", ev.Type)

ChatResult provides top-level fields for content, provider, model, request ID, cost in micro-dollars, routing time in microseconds, cache status, and whether a fallback was attempted. Usage and Raw expose internal domain types; prefer the top-level fields when you need a stable public SDK surface. For function/tool definitions and the HTTP request shape, see Tool Calling. The current public ChatRequest struct does not expose a tools field.
The pkg/gateway package uses functional options to configure an embedded gateway or a remote gateway client.

Initializes a client. If WithRemote(...) is provided, it connects to that remote service. Otherwise, it loads configuration and starts an embedded gateway server in the current process: gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList( gateway.ModelEntry{ModelName: "fast", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"}, ), gateway.WithLogLevel("info"), ) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("failed to initialize: %v", err) } defer gw.Close()
Creates an HTTP client pointing to an already-running GoRoute server or container: client := gateway.NewClient("http://localhost:8080", "sk-gw-developer-key")

Configures the embedded router with declarative model aliases, fallbacks, and routing strategies. gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList( gateway.ModelEntry{ ModelName: "smart-router", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", APIKey: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY", RoutingStrategy: "least-busy", Fallbacks: []string{"backup-claude"}, RPM: 1000, TPM: 500000, }, gateway.ModelEntry{ ModelName: "backup-claude", Model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514", APIKey: "os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", }, ), ) ModelEntry Specification​ Field Type Description ModelName string Client-facing alias (e.g. "fast", "reasoning", "auto"). Model string Upstream provider/model identifier (e.g. "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"). APIKey string Upstream API key string or environment reference (e.g. "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY"). APIBase string Optional custom endpoint URL (e.g. for Ollama or private vLLM clusters: "http://localhost:11434"). RoutingStrategy string Routing policy: "weighted-shuffle", "least-busy", "latency-based", "usage-based-headroom", "lowest-cost", or "round-robin". Fallbacks []string Ordered list of model aliases to invoke if this model returns 429, 503, or times out. Weight int Integer weight for "weighted-shuffle" distribution. RPM int Requests Per Minute limit enforced across this model entry. TPM int Tokens Per Minute limit enforced across this model entry. SimulateStatus int Optional fault injection HTTP code (e.g. 503) to test circuit breakers and fallback chains offline.

Loads model definitions, rate limits, and security policies from an external YAML file: gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithConfigFile("./config/gateway.yaml"), ) Sample YAML (gateway.yaml): model_list: - model_name: "production-fast" model_params: model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash" api_key: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY" rpm: 1000 fallbacks: ["production-backup"] - model_name: "production-backup" model_params: model: "openai/gpt-4.1-mini" api_key: "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"

Enables built-in local mock HTTP servers for any ModelEntry whose environment variable API key is not present. This allows unit tests, integration tests, and local demos to run immediately without requiring live provider credentials or incurring costs. gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList( gateway.ModelEntry{ModelName: "test-model", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"}, ), gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), // Mock provider handles requests locally )

Control internal gateway logging using Go standard library's log/slog: WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option: Provide a custom slog.Logger instance. WithSilentLogs() Option: Suppress all stdout/stderr logs (ideal for CLI tools or clean terminal outputs). WithLogLevel(level string) Option: Set minimum log level ("debug", "info", "warn", "error"). customLogger := slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelDebug})) gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithLogger(customLogger), )
Redirects gateway.New to connect to a remote gateway daemon instead of starting an embedded router: gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithRemote("https://ai-gateway.company.com", "sk-gw-production"), )

Configures a custom *http.Client for remote gateway HTTP requests and /v1/realtime WebSocket dialing (timeouts, custom TLS, transport pooling): customHTTP := &http.Client{Timeout: 45 * time.Second} gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithRemote("https://ai-gateway.company.com", "sk-gw-production"), gateway.WithHTTPClient(customHTTP), )
Permits embedded gateway connections to localhost or private network addresses (useful for local Ollama/LM Studio servers or in-process test mocks without enabling WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing()).

In multi-tenant backend services, create a shallow copy of the client with a tenant's specific Virtual API Key. The base connection and connection pooling are shared: // Base client initialized once at service startup masterClient, _ := gateway.New(...) // HTTP handler for tenant A func TenantAHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { tenantKey := r.Header.Get("X-Tenant-Key") tenantClient := masterClient.WithKey(tenantKey) // Chat requests are now governed by tenantKey's budget, rate limits, and model allowances res, err := tenantClient.Chat(r.Context(), "fast", "Process tenant query") ... }

For embedded instances, Close() cleanly shuts down background workers, flushes remaining telemetry events, and terminates local mock servers: defer gw.Close() (For remote clients created via NewClient, Close() is a safe no-op).
Inspect the loopback HTTP URL generated for the in-process server (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:54321): fmt.Printf("Embedded gateway listening internally on: %s\n", gw.BaseURL())

documents.s: Virtual keys, governance, FinOps & protocol registration

documents.t: The SDK includes public configuration types for registering MCP servers and A2A agents. The gateway exposes the protocol routes for tool calls, agent messages, and tasks. Administrative registration methods require a client authenticated with an admin key and the corresponding server permissions.

serverID, err := gw.AddMCPServer(ctx, gateway.MCPServerConfig{ Name: "Example tools", Slug: "example-tools", Transport: "streamable_http", URL: "https://tools.example.com/mcp", Enabled: true, }) if err != nil { return err } toolCount, err := gw.SyncMCPTools(ctx, serverID) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Printf("Synced %d tools\n", toolCount) The gateway applies outbound network policy to the MCP server URL. Confirm the transport and endpoint path expected by your MCP server before registering it.
documents.s: Register and sync an MCP server

documents.t: ListMCPTools accepts an empty route for the virtual hub, a server slug, or a toolsets/{slug} route: tools, err := gw.ListMCPTools(ctx, "example-tools") if err != nil { return err } for _, tool := range tools { fmt.Println(tool["name"], tool["description"]) } The gateway also provides a plain REST bridge for clients that do not use JSON-RPC. See the MCP overview, hub and REST bridge, and MCP API reference.

agentID, err := gw.AddA2AAgent(ctx, gateway.A2AAgentConfig{ Name: "Research agent", Slug: "research", Description: "Internal research agent", EndpointURL: "https://agent.example.com", }) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println("Registered agent:", agentID) Use GetWellKnownAgentCard(ctx) to fetch the gateway's signed discovery card (/.well-known/agent-card.json), and consult the A2A API reference for message and task request schemas. The SDK's SendA2AMessage method currently accepts a protobuf type from an internal package, so applications outside the gateway module should use the HTTP API or another supported public client for dispatch.

Use an admin client only for registration and management calls; use scoped virtual keys for application traffic. Allow only destinations that should receive gateway requests, and review the outbound SSRF/network policy. Disable Stdio MCP servers unless the gateway configuration and deployment are prepared to allow them.

Package: github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway. The SDK provides a Go client for chat requests and common gateway operations. It can start a gateway instance in the current process or connect to an HTTP gateway service.

Mode Constructor What it does Embedded gateway.New(...) Loads gateway configuration, starts an in-process gateway server, and returns a client that talks to it over HTTP. Remote gateway.NewClient(url, key) or gateway.WithRemote(url, key) Sends requests to an already running gateway service. The embedded mode does not require a separately deployed gateway service. It still runs the gateway server and uses HTTP internally; it is not a direct function call into the inference handler.
The upstream module currently declares Go 1.26.0 in go.mod. Use a compatible Go toolchain: go get github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway@v1.7.0

ctx := context.Background() gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList(gateway.ModelEntry{ ModelName: "fast", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", APIKey: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY", }), gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), ) if err != nil { return err } defer gw.Close() result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Explain what an AI gateway does.") if err != nil { return err } fmt.Println(result.Content) This is a function-body example; it assumes context, fmt, and the gateway package are imported and is inside a function that can return an error. The mock option provides a local fallback when the referenced environment key is unset. To verify a real provider call, configure a valid key and omit the mock option.
Client configuration Chat and streaming Virtual keys and FinOps MCP and A2A Public SDK types and methods

The SDK provides methods for creating and revoking virtual keys and reading the spend summary. These are administrative operations: use a client configured with the gateway admin credential and protect it as a privileged object.

key, err := adminClient.CreateVirtualKey(ctx, gateway.VirtualKeyRequest{ Name: "payments-service", OrgID: "org_default", Role: "service_account", MaxBudgetMicros: 25_000_000, // 25 USD RPMLimit: 120, TPMLimit: 100_000, AllowedModels: []string{"fast"}, }) if err != nil { return err } // Store key.Key in an approved secret store; do not log or commit it. fmt.Println("Created key ID:", key.ID) MaxBudgetMicros uses micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000 µ$). The returned key.Key contains the new secret and is only available in the creation response. Store it securely.

For server-controlled application code, create a request client using the virtual key: tenantClient := gateway.NewClient(gatewayURL, key.Key) result, err := tenantClient.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Summarize the supplied text.") WithKey can also copy a client with a different inference key. Keep any client carrying an admin credential inside trusted server code: the copy retains the original admin key for administrative methods.

if err := adminClient.RevokeVirtualKey(ctx, key.ID); err != nil { return err } The SDK calls the gateway's revoke endpoint. Subsequent authentication behavior depends on the gateway version and cache propagation; check the response and logs if a key still appears active.

Use GetSpendSummary (added in v1.7.0) for a pure-SDK *gateway.SpendSummaryResponse with zero internal/ package dependencies: summary, err := adminClient.GetSpendSummary(ctx) if err != nil { return err } fmt.Printf("Requests: %d; tokens: %d; cost: %d µ$ ($%.4f; unpriced: %d)\n", summary.TotalRequests, summary.TotalTokens, summary.TotalCostMicros, summary.TotalCostUSD, summary.UnpricedRequests) fmt.Println("Spend by provider:", summary.SpendByProvider) The SDK also exposes UpdateVirtualKey, RotateVirtualKey, UpdateTeam, DeleteTeam, UpdateUser, DeleteUser, and GetConfig using public SDK types, plus the legacy SpendSummary method (which returns an internal storage type). The stable JSON API is available at GET /admin/v1/spend/summary; see the cost accounting guide and Admin API reference.

GoRoute is engineered as an Enterprise AI Control Plane written in pure Go, organizing traffic routing, security governance, micro-dollar FinOps, observability, and agent management into five cohesive modules on top of a lock-free Go core and distributed persistence layer. It delivers sub-2ms hot-path routing overhead, multi-tenant isolation, and resilient upstream execution. GoRoute Enterprise AI Control Plane (Pure Go) Go Core & Persistence Layer Clients, IDEs & Agents(OpenAI / Anthropic SDKs, Claude Code, Cursor, MCP, A2A) 1. AI Gateway(/v1/*, 73 Providers,EWMA, Circuit Breakers) 2. AI Governance(4-Layer RBAC, Vault,Guardrails, SSRF) 3. AI FinOps(Micro-Dollar Ledger,Outboxes, Lua Limits) 4. AI Observability(OTLP, Prometheus,Operator UI /ui/) 5. AI Agent Mgmt(MCP Hub, A2A gRPC,Tool Loops) L1 In-Memory Cache(Ring Buffers & Auth) Redis UniversalClient(Cluster/Sentinel, Lua, Pub/Sub) PostgreSQL 16+(Migrations 0001-0015, Outboxes) [!NOTE] GoRoute's architecture eliminates synchronous PostgreSQL queries on the inference hot path using an L1 In-Memory + L2 Redis caching topology, single-roundtrip Redis Lua rate limiters, and asynchronous batched PostgreSQL spend pipelines.

You can install and spin up the complete GoRoute AI Gateway binary in seconds: # 1. Download and install the precompiled binary curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash # 2. Run the gateway with your configuration ai-gateway --config config/gateway.yaml Once running, access the embedded visual administration dashboard: http://localhost:8080/ui/ The Operator UI lets you observe real-time inference latency, view active deployment health states, configure virtual keys, simulate guardrails, and run interactive streaming sessions.

Every inference request traversing GoRoute undergoes a deterministic 10-step lifecycle: Cache HIT Cache MISS Client Request(OpenAI SDK / Go SDK / cURL) 1. Auth and Vault(SHA-256 Virtual Key, 4-Layer RBAC) 2. Distributed Rate Limiter(Redis Lua Sliding Window RPM/TPM) 3. Exact Cache(Deterministic SHA-256)? 4. Return Cached Response(0.05ms Fast Path) 5. Stage 1 Heuristic Classifier(Sub-0.1ms Zero-LLM Fast vs Reasoning) 6. Stage 2 EWMA Load Balancer(6 Strategies) 7. 3-State Circuit Breakers(Healthy / Half-Open / Open) 8. Wire Protocol Normalization(Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, Mistral, Ollama) 9. Model Execution and SSE Stream 10. Asynchronous FinOps Ledger(Integer Micro-Dollars, pgx.Batch)

The incoming Bearer token (sk-gw-...) is hashed using SHA-256. The token digest is verified against an in-memory L1 cache (15-second TTL) or Redis L2 cache. The gateway resolves the caller's multi-tenant context: Organization ID, Team ID, User ID, Virtual Key scopes, and micro-dollar budget balances. Outbound upstream provider credentials remain strictly isolated inside the AES-256-GCM encrypted credentials vault.

Executes an atomic Redis Lua script implementing a sliding-window counter. Enforces both Requests Per Minute (RPM) and preflight estimated Tokens Per Minute (TPM). If limits are reached, immediately returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a precise Retry-After header.

Computes a deterministic SHA-256 cache key across {TenantID, Model, SystemPrompt, Messages, Tools}. Deterministic queries (temperature: 0.0) resulting in a cache hit bypass the router and upstream providers entirely, returning in <0.05ms with zero token cost.

When the logical model alias model: "auto" is requested, GoRoute evaluates prompt complexity in under 0.1ms without invoking costly secondary LLMs: Measures token volume and conversational turn depth. Detects programming language keywords (func, class, import, SQL statements, backticks). Scans for algorithmic, logical, and mathematical reasoning terms. Simple tasks route to lightweight aliases (fast); complex tasks route to reasoning tiers (reasoning). Configure each alias with model IDs that are available to your provider account and exposed by the gateway catalog. The model behind an alias can change without changing the client request.

Selects the target provider deployment using one of six strategies: weighted-shuffle: Proportional weighted random distribution. least-busy: Routes to the deployment with the fewest active in-flight requests. latency-based: Routes based on exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) latency. usage-based-headroom: Dynamically shifts traffic based on remaining RPM/TPM headroom. lowest-cost: Prioritizes deployments with the lowest micro-dollar unit cost. round-robin: Distributes requests evenly across deployments using a per-group atomic counter.

Tracks upstream health through a finite state machine: CLOSED (Healthy), OPEN (Tripped), and HALF_OPEN (Trial). Three consecutive 5xx errors or network timeouts trip the circuit breaker, diverting subsequent requests immediately without waiting for timeouts.

When an upstream fails, GoRoute automatically traverses configured fallback model groups (e.g., Primary OpenAI → Secondary Anthropic Claude → Tertiary Google Gemini). Requests are retried with exponential backoff and decorrelated jitter.

Translates canonical gateway request schemas into vendor-specific payloads: OpenAI: Maps developer/system messages and tool schemas. Anthropic Claude: Consolidates parallel tool calls into strict alternating user/assistant turns and maps thinking token budgets. Google Gemini: Converts message arrays into Gemini contents with thinkingConfig. Ollama: Generates local JSON payloads.

Server-Sent Events (SSE) emitted by upstream models are parsed on the fly. Chunks are forwarded directly to the HTTP response flusher with zero memory buffering, maintaining real-time Time-To-First-Token (TTFT).

Token usage is priced using integer micro-dollars ($1.00 USD = 1,000,000 µ$) to eliminate floating-point rounding errors. Spend events are placed onto a lock-free in-memory ring buffer. A background worker flushes events to PostgreSQL in batched pgx.Batch transactions, keeping the data plane latency unaffected.

GoRoute implements enterprise governance across 4 hierarchical evaluation layers: [Layer 1: Global Model Catalogue] │ (Discovered and registered provider models; availability varies by deployment) ▼ [Layer 2: Organization Subscriptions] │ (Admin enables specific cloud providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) ▼ [Layer 3: Organization Model Policies] │ (Org-wide availability overrides and max token ceilings) ▼ [Layer 4: Virtual Key Allowlists] │ (Scoped API key model permissions: e.g. ["fast", "gemini-2.5-flash"]) ▼ [Execution Allowed] [!IMPORTANT] If a model is not permitted at any of the 4 layers, GoRoute fails closed with an explicit HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 404 Model Not Found.

GoRoute provides unified routing across three core protocols: OpenAI-Compatible Data Plane (/v1/*): Supports standard chat completions, embeddings, audio, images, files, batches, and realtime WebSockets. Model Context Protocol (/mcp/*, /mcp-rest/*): Serves as a central virtual hub aggregating distributed MCP tool servers with schema validation and progressive discovery. Agent-to-Agent Protocol (/a2a/v1/*): Provides RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized and RFC 7515 JWS signed Agent Cards, asynchronous task state machines, and native gRPC streaming. Access all configured protocols and live health metrics via the Operator Web UI.

GoRoute is a high-throughput, low-overhead Enterprise AI Control Plane engineered in pure Go. It unifies 73 ProviderType profiles (plus CustomOpenAICompatible), 23 primary /v1 data plane paths (26 HTTP operations), a Model Context Protocol (MCP 2026-07-28) virtual hub, and a Linux Foundation Agent-to-Agent (A2A v1.0) bridge into five integrated control-plane modules: AI Gateway — Traffic Management & Model Routing: Multi-provider /v1/* and /anthropic/v1/* data plane (23 primary /v1 paths / 26 operations), SupportedOperations enforcement, Stage 1 complexity classifier, Stage 2 load balancers (6 strategies including round-robin), 3-state Redis circuit breakers, bounded fallback chains, and 2-tier exact-match caching. AI Governance — Security, Policies & Compliance: 4-layer access hierarchy, Operator RBAC + OIDC/JWT, AES-256-GCM Credentials Vault, scoped Virtual Keys (sk-gw-...), streaming & logging_only guardrails, outbound SSRF firewall, and HTTP security headers. AI FinOps — Cost Management & Optimization: 64-bit integer micro-dollar ledger ($1 = 1,000,000 µ$), cache-write & modality pricing (0007/0012), unpriced_requests tracking, pre-flight upper-bound budget reservations, durable PostgreSQL spend & budget-reset outboxes (0008/0011/0014), Redis Lua rate limits, and pre-flight tokenization. AI Observability — Monitoring, Tracing & Evaluation: OTLP/HTTP distributed tracing (gen_ai.*, W3C traceparent), Prometheus /metrics, Vitter Algorithm R latency reservoirs, Embedded Operator Console (/ui/*), Guardrails Policy Simulator, and secret-scrubbed slog logs. AI Agent Management — MCP, Tools & Agent Access: MCP Virtual Hub, REST bridge (/mcp-rest/*), progressive discovery, sandboxed Stdio & SHA-256 tool pinning, MRTR AEAD tokens, A2A signed Agent Cards (JCS/JWS) & native gRPC, autonomous tool loops, and coding-agent/framework access control. [!NOTE] GoRoute compiles into a single, self-contained static binary with zero external runtime dependencies. An embedded Operator Web UI is served directly from the gateway at http://localhost:8080/ui/.

Install the latest precompiled GoRoute binary for your OS (macOS, Linux, Windows) and architecture (amd64, arm64) using the universal shell installer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash To install a specific version pin (such as v1.7.0): curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v1.7.0 [!TIP] The installer automatically verifies SHA-256 checksums, selects /usr/local/bin (or ~/.local/bin), and validates executable permissions.

Choose the deployment architecture that fits your infrastructure requirements: Deployment Mode Description Best Suited For Quickstart Guide Standalone CLI Service Pre-compiled binary running as an independent HTTP/gRPC daemon. Microservices, VMs, multi-language stacks (Python, Node.js, Rust). Gateway Quickstart Docker Compose Orchestrated local stack including PostgreSQL 16+ and Redis 7+. GoRoute embeds a rich single-page management application directly inside the binary. Once the gateway is running, navigate to: http://localhost:8080/ui/ Authenticate using your Master Admin Key (GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY). The Operator UI provides real-time access to: Streaming Chat Playground: Test model groups, dynamic routes, and reasoning parameters with live token metrics. Model Catalogue & Routing: Inspect the models available to your deployment, configure aliases (fast, reasoning), and tune load balancers. Model availability depends on provider access, catalog sync, organization policy, and key permissions. Virtual API Keys: Issue tenant-scoped keys with RPM/TPM rate limits, budget caps, and model allowlists. FinOps Ledger: Monitor micro-dollar expenditure, token breakdowns, and team cost attribution. Guardrails Simulator: Interactively evaluate regex PII redaction and secret scanning rules without model invocations. Credentials Vault: Securely manage and test encrypted provider API credentials. Agentic Hub: Audit active MCP servers, progressive tool catalogs, and A2A agents.

HIT MISS Client Request(OpenAI SDK / cURL / MCP) GoRoute Gateway(:8080) Virtual Key Authand 4-Layer RBAC Redis Lua Limiter(Sliding RPM / TPM) Exact Cache(SHA-256 HIT?) Immediate Response(0.05ms) Two-Stage Router(Classifier + Balancer) Circuit Breakerand Fallback Cascade Winning Provider(OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, etc.) FinOps Ledger(Micro-Dollar Accounting) Every inference request traversing GoRoute undergoes sub-2ms processing on the hot path: Dual-Boundary Authentication: Caller credentials (sk-gw-...) are resolved via L1/L2 caches and strictly separated from outbound provider API keys. Distributed Rate Limiting: Atomic Redis Lua sliding windows enforce per-key RPM and estimated TPM limits before reaching upstreams. Deterministic Exact-Match Caching: Zero-cost, sub-millisecond responses for cached deterministic prompts (temperature: 0.0). Intelligent Model Selection: Heuristic Stage 1 classification and Stage 2 load balancing choose the fastest, most cost-effective deployment. Resilient Execution: 3-state circuit breakers divert traffic on upstream failure, walking configured fallback cascades automatically. FinOps Micro-Dollar Ledger: Asynchronous token and cost accounting persists to PostgreSQL via batch pipelines without delaying the client stream.

23 Primary /v1 Data Plane Paths (26 HTTP Operations): Unified endpoints for Chat Completions, Text Completions, Vector Embeddings, Reranking, Moderation, Anthropic Messages, Tokenization, Audio (STT & TTS), Image Generation/Edits/Variations, Stateful Tenant Files, Asynchronous Batches, Responses API, and Realtime WebSockets. 73 ProviderType Profiles: Native adapters for dedicated cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Cohere, Mistral, Ollama), 60+ built-in and extended OpenAI-compatible dialect profiles, and CustomOpenAICompatible. Agentic Protocols Built-In: Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) virtual hub with tool deduplication and progressive discovery, alongside Linux Foundation Agent-to-Agent (A2A) cryptographic cards, message dispatch, and gRPC streaming. Enterprise FinOps: Real-time micro-dollar ledger ($1 = 1,000,000 µ$) with multi-tenant budgeting, spend summaries, and immutable audit logs. Multi-Tenant Security: 4-layer access hierarchy (public catalogue → org subscriptions → org model policy → virtual key allowlist) with automated PII masking and secret redaction.

Choose the path that matches what you are building — embed GoRoute inside a Go service, run it as a shared HTTP/gRPC gateway, or govern tools and coding agents: Path A — Build a Go Application (pkg/gateway): Start with the Go SDK Overview and Go SDK Quickstart, configure model aliases in Client Configuration, add streaming via Chat and Streaming, and explore Go Examples. Path B — Run a Shared Gateway: Choose between the Standalone Gateway Quickstart and Docker Compose Quickstart, tune Configuration and Storage, connect Providers, and verify Observability & Health Probes and the Production Checklist. Path C — Connect Tools, Agents & Coding IDEs: Configure the MCP Virtual Hub and A2A Protocol, compare with MCP and A2A in the Go SDK, or point Integrations (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs) at your gateway.

Run GoRoute AI Gateway in a fully containerized production topology with PostgreSQL 16+ for persistent multi-tenant metadata and Redis 7+ for distributed sliding-window rate limiting. [!NOTE] If you prefer a lightweight single-binary host installation rather than containers, use the one-line shell installer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash
Docker Engine 24.0+ and Docker Compose v2.20+. Valid API keys for upstream LLM providers (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY) or a local Ollama instance.

Clone the repository and inspect the deployment manifest: git clone https://github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go.git cd ai-gateway-go The stack is defined in deployments/docker-compose.yml: version: "3.9" services: gateway: build: context: .. dockerfile: deployments/Dockerfile ports: - "8080:8080" environment: - GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY=sk-gw-master-admin-default-key-change-me - GATEWAY_STORAGE_MODE=postgres - DATABASE_URL=postgres://goroute:goroute_secret@postgres:5432/goroute_db?sslmode=disable - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0 - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY:-} - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-} - GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY:-} depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy redis: condition: service_healthy postgres: image: postgres:16-alpine environment: POSTGRES_USER: goroute POSTGRES_PASSWORD: goroute_secret POSTGRES_DB: goroute_db ports: - "5432:5432" volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data healthcheck: test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U goroute -d goroute_db"] interval: 5s timeout: 5s retries: 5 redis: image: redis:7-alpine ports: - "6379:6379" volumes: - redisdata:/data healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"] interval: 5s timeout: 5s retries: 5 volumes: pgdata: redisdata:

documents.t: Start the gateway, database, and cache containers in the background: docker compose -f deployments/docker-compose.yml up -d --build View startup logs to confirm automated database migrations and route registrations: docker compose -f deployments/docker-compose.yml logs -f gateway

Once the containers are running and healthy, open the Operator Web UI in your browser: http://localhost:8080/ui/ Log in with the configured master admin key: sk-gw-master-admin-default-key-change-me [!IMPORTANT] The default development key sk-gw-master-admin-default-key-change-me must be replaced with a high-entropy secret before deploying to staging or production environments. The Operator UI gives you complete control over: Live multi-provider chat playgrounds with streaming SSE. Real-time token consumption, request latencies, and micro-dollar FinOps balances. Automated health state machine inspections (CLOSED, HALF_OPEN, OPEN). Interactive guardrail policy simulation and PII redaction checks.

Execute an OpenAI-compatible request against the running Docker stack: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-master-admin-default-key-change-me" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "fast", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain containerized microservices."} ], "stream": false }'
Verify that both PostgreSQL and Redis are responsive through GoRoute's deep readiness check: curl http://localhost:8080/readyz Expected response (HTTP 200 OK): { "status": "ready" }

To shut down the stack while preserving data volumes: docker compose -f deployments/docker-compose.yml down To purge persistent volumes as well: docker compose -f deployments/docker-compose.yml down -v
Consult the Operator UI Runbook for administration workflows. Explore the Admin Control Plane API for automated provisioning. Learn about Distributed Rate Limiting using Redis Lua scripts.

Run GoRoute AI Gateway as a high-performance standalone service to provide an intelligent, multi-provider AI proxy for your engineering team or microservices architecture. [!NOTE] GoRoute runs as a single static binary with no external interpreter dependencies. It includes an embedded Operator Web UI accessible directly at http://localhost:8080/ui/.

Install the compiled binary directly to /usr/local/bin (or ~/.local/bin): curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash To install a specific release version: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v1.5.0 Verify the installation: ai-gateway -version
If you have Go 1.26+ installed: git clone https://github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go.git cd ai-gateway-go go build -o ai-gateway ./cmd/gateway

Create a minimal configuration file config.yaml or use the provided template: server: port: 8080 host: "0.0.0.0" auth: master_admin_key: "sk-gw-admin-secret-key-12345" storage: mode: "memory" # Use "postgres" for persistent multi-tenant production providers: openai: api_key: "env.OPENAI_API_KEY" anthropic: api_key: "env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" gemini: api_key: "env.GEMINI_API_KEY" ollama: base_url: "http://localhost:11434" model_groups: - name: "fast" routing_strategy: "weighted-shuffle" deployments: - provider: "gemini" model: "gemini-2.5-flash" weight: 60 - provider: "openai" model: "gpt-4o-mini" weight: 40 - name: "reasoning" routing_strategy: "latency-based" deployments: - provider: "anthropic" model: "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022" weight: 100 [!TIP] Provider API keys can be passed directly as environment variables or referenced dynamically with env.VARIABLE_NAME.
Launch the service pointing to your configuration file: ./ai-gateway -config config.yaml The gateway immediately initializes routes, background workers, and the embedded Operator Web UI on port 8080.

Open your browser and navigate to: http://localhost:8080/ui/ When prompted, log in with your master admin key: sk-gw-admin-secret-key-12345 From the Operator UI, you can: Test real-time streaming completions in the Chat Playground. Monitor live token spend and request latencies in Overview. Inspect active upstream deployments and circuit breaker states in Models & Routing. Provision new Virtual API Keys for applications and developers in Virtual Keys.

Send an inference request using standard OpenAI cURL format: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-admin-secret-key-12345" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "fast", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise Go systems engineer."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Explain how GoRoute manages sub-2ms routing overhead."} ], "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 150 }'

GoRoute returns rich telemetry and accounting headers on every request: HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json X-Gateway-Request-Id: req_991efda4-7fab-4b03 X-Trace-Id: bad98e7deea34d7c810a963d9ed2c4ef X-Gateway-Provider: gemini X-Gateway-Model: gemini-2.5-flash X-Gateway-Cost-Micros: 45 X-Gateway-Routing-Time: 12 µs X-Gateway-Cache: MISS

Check process health probes: # Liveness probe curl http://localhost:8080/healthz # Readiness probe (validates database and Redis connections) curl http://localhost:8080/readyz # Prometheus metrics curl http://localhost:8080/metrics
Explore the complete API Reference for all 21 data plane endpoints. Configure Virtual Keys & RBAC for tenant management. Set up Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis.

Use the Go SDK to run an embedded gateway in your Go process or connect to a gateway that is already running. This guide shows the embedded option and uses local mock providers when a provider key is unavailable.
Go 1.26 or newer. A provider API key for a live request. Without one, the example uses the SDK's mock provider option.
From your Go module: go get github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway@v1.5.0 Set a provider key if you want to send requests to a real provider: export GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-api-key"

Create main.go: package main import ( "context" "fmt" "log" "github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway" ) func main() { ctx := context.Background() gw, err := gateway.New( gateway.WithModelList(gateway.ModelEntry{ ModelName: "fast", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash", APIKey: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY", }), gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), ) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } defer gw.Close() result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Explain what an AI gateway does in one sentence.", gateway.WithMaxTokens(128), ) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } fmt.Printf("[%s] %s\n", result.Provider, result.Content) fmt.Printf("Cost: %d micro-dollars; routing: %d µs\n", result.CostMicros, result.RoutingMicros) } Run it: go run . With no GEMINI_API_KEY, WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing supplies a local mock for this model. The mock is useful for trying the SDK flow; it does not verify provider credentials or live provider behavior.

The public SDK request type is ChatRequest; use ChatWithMessages for structured conversations: result, err := gw.ChatWithMessages(ctx, gateway.ChatRequest{ Model: "fast", Messages: []gateway.Message{ {Role: "system", Content: "You are a concise Go tutor."}, {Role: "user", Content: "What does context cancellation do?"}, }, }) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } fmt.Println(result.Content)

StreamChat invokes the callback as text deltas arrive and returns the aggregated result when the stream ends: _, err = gw.StreamChat(ctx, "fast", "Write a short haiku about Go.", func(delta string) error { fmt.Print(delta) return nil }) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } fmt.Println()

Use NewClient when a gateway daemon is already running: client := gateway.NewClient("http://localhost:8080", "sk-gw-your-virtual-key") result, err := client.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Hello from a remote Go client.")
